positive_text: Un număr natural se numește circular dacă numărul divizorilor săi este un pătrat perfect. Fie $n$ un astfel de număr cu $d^2$ divizori, pe care îi așezăm într-un tablou pătrat $d \times d$. La fiecare pas, alegem un rând și rotim toate elementele acestuia cu o poziție la dreapta (ultimul element ajungând pe prima poziție). O configurație este considerată acceptabilă dacă există o coloană în care elementele sunt în șir crescător sau descrescător prin divizibilitate (adică $a_1 \mid a_2 \mid \ldots \mid a_d$ sau $a_d \mid a_{d-1} \mid \ldots \mid a_1$). Găsiți toate numerele circulare $n \geq 2$ pentru care, indiferent de modul inițial de așezare a divizorilor în tablou, putem ajunge printr-un număr finit de rotații la o configurație acceptabilă.

negatives.text: Un număr natural se numește rotund dacă numărul divizorilor săi este un pătrat perfect. Fie $n$ un astfel de număr cu $d^2$ divizori, pe care îi așezăm într-un tablou pătrat $d \times d$. La fiecare pas, alegem un rând și înmulțim fiecare element al acestuia cu 2. O configurație este considerată acceptabilă dacă există o coloană în care elementele sunt în șir crescător sau descrescător prin divizibilitate (adică $a_1 \mid a_2 \mid \ldots \mid a_d$ sau $a_d \mid a_{d-1} \mid \ldots \mid a_1$). Găsiți toate numerele rotunde $n \geq 2$ pentru care, indiferent de modul inițial de așezare a divizorilor în tablou, putem ajunge printr-un număr finit de operații la o configurație acceptabilă.

Un număr natural se numește rotund dacă numărul divizorilor săi este un pătrat perfect. Fie $n$ un astfel de număr cu $d^2$ divizori, pe care îi așezăm într-un tablou pătrat $d \times d$. La fiecare pas, alegem un rând și putem schimba două elemente din acel rând între ele. O configurație este considerată acceptabilă dacă există o coloană în care elementele sunt în șir crescător sau descrescător prin divizibilitate (adică $a_1 \mid a_2 \mid \ldots \mid a_d$ sau $a_d \mid a_{d-1} \mid \ldots \mid a_1$). Găsiți toate numerele rotunde $n \geq 2$ pentru care, indiferent de modul inițial de așezare a divizorilor în tablou, putem ajunge printr-un număr finit de operații la o configurație acceptabilă.

positive_text:
Determine all real values of $k$ such that the equation
$$
\sqrt{k x^{2} + k x + 2} = k x + 2
$$
has exactly one solution.

negatives.text:
Find all values of $a$ for which the equation
$$
\sqrt{a x^{2} + a x + 2} = a x - 2
$$
has a unique root.

Find all values of $a$ for which the equation
$$
\sqrt{a x^{2} + a x + 2} = x + 2
$$
has a unique root.

Find all values of $a$ for which the equation
$$
\sqrt{a x^{2} + a x + 2} = a x + 2
$$
has a unique positive root.

positive_text:
Among $n$ identical items, three are faulty. A diagnostic tool checks subsets of items and reports if 0, 1, or more than 1 are faulty. Let $L(n)$ be the minimal number of tests needed to identify the three faulty items.

a) Determine $L(6)$.

b) Show that $L(n) \leq \frac{n+5}{2}$.

negatives.text:
Among $n$ identical items, one is faulty. A diagnostic tool checks subsets of items and reports if 0 or 1 is faulty. Let $L(n)$ be the minimal number of tests needed to identify the single faulty item.

a) Determine $L(6)$.

b) Show that $L(n) \leq \frac{n+5}{2}$.

Among $n$ identical items, three are faulty. A diagnostic tool checks subsets of items and reports only whether 0 or more than 0 are faulty. Let $L(n)$ be the minimal number of tests needed to identify the three faulty items.

a) Determine $L(6)$.

b) Show that $L(n) \leq \frac{n+5}{2}$.

positive_text:
Let $b \geq 2$ be a real number. Let $r_{1}$ and $r_{2}$ be the roots of the quadratic $x^{2}-b x+1=0$, and define $T_{n} = r_{1}^{n} + r_{2}^{n}$ for $n=1,2,\ldots$

a) Show that the sequence $\left\{\frac{T_{n}}{T_{n+1}}\right\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is strictly decreasing.

b) Determine all $b$ for which the inequality
$$
\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}+\frac{T_{2}}{T_{3}}+\cdots+\frac{T_{n}}{T_{n+1}} > n-1
$$
holds for all positive integers $n$.

negatives.text:
Let $a \geq 2$ be a real number. Let $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ be the roots of $x^{2}-a x+1=0$, and define $S_{n} = x_{1}^{n} - x_{2}^{n}$, $n=1,2,\ldots$

a) Prove that the sequence $\left\{\frac{S_{n}}{S_{n+1}}\right\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is decreasing.

b) Find all $a$ such that
$$
\frac{S_{1}}{S_{2}}+\frac{S_{2}}{S_{3}}+\cdots+\frac{S_{n}}{S_{n+1}} > n-1
$$
for all positive integers $n$.

Let $a \geq 2$ be a real number. Let $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ be the roots of $x^{2}-a x+1=0$, and define $S_{n} = x_{1}^{n} + x_{2}^{n}$, $n=1,2,\ldots$

a) Prove that the sequence $\left\{\frac{S_{n}}{S_{n+1}}\right\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is increasing.

b) Find all $a$ such that
$$
\frac{S_{1}}{S_{2}}+\frac{S_{2}}{S_{3}}+\cdots+\frac{S_{n}}{S_{n+1}} < n-1
$$
for all positive integers $n$.

Let $a \geq 2$ be a real number. Let $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ be the roots of $x^{2}-a x+1=0$, and define $S_{n} = x_{1}^{n} + x_{2}^{n}$, $n=1,2,\ldots$

a) Prove that the sequence $\left\{\frac{S_{n}}{S_{n+1}}\right\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is decreasing.

b) Find all $a$ such that
$$
\frac{S_{1}}{S_{2}}+\frac{S_{2}}{S_{3}}+\cdots+\frac{S_{n}}{S_{n+1}} > n
$$
for all positive integers $n$.

positive_text: Let $ P $ be a point inside triangle $ XYZ $. The lines $ XP $, $ YP $, and $ ZP $ meet the sides $ YZ $, $ ZX $, and $ XY $ at points $ X_1 $, $ Y_1 $, and $ Z_1 $, respectively. Suppose that $ S_{ZY_1P} = 2 S_{XZ_1P} $. Prove that $ X_1 $ is the midpoint of $ YZ $ if and only if $ S_{YX_1P} = 3 S_{XZ_1P} $.

negatives.text: Let $ M $ be an interior point of $ \triangle ABC $. The lines $ AM $, $ BM $, and $ CM $ meet the lines $ BC $, $ CA $, and $ AB $ at points $ A_1 $, $ B_1 $, and $ C_1 $, respectively. Suppose that $ S_{CB_1M} = 2 S_{AC_1M} $. Prove that $ A_1 $ is the midpoint of $ BC $ if and only if $ S_{CA_1M} = 3 S_{AC_1M} $.

Let $ M $ be an interior point of $ \triangle ABC $. The lines $ AM $, $ BM $, and $ CM $ meet the lines $ BC $, $ CA $, and $ AB $ at points $ A_1 $, $ B_1 $, and $ C_1 $, respectively. Suppose that $ S_{CB_1M} = 2 S_{AC_1M} $. Prove that $ A_1 $ is the midpoint of $ BC $ if and only if $ S_{BA_1M} = 2 S_{AC_1M} $.

positive_text:
Let
$$
h(x) = \frac{\cos^2 x}{1 + \cos x + \cos^2 x} \text{ and } p(x) = k \tan x + (1-k) \sin x - x
$$
with $k$ being a real constant.

a) Show that $p'(x) = \frac{(1-\cos x)(k-h(x))}{h(x)}$.

b) Determine the range of $h(x)$ for $x \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

c) Find all real values of $k$ for which $p(x) \geq 0$ for all $x \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

negatives.text:
Let
$$
h(x) = \frac{\cos^2 x}{1 + \cos x + \cos^2 x} \text{ and } p(x) = k \tan x + (1-k) \sin^2 x - x
$$
with $k$ being a real constant.

a) Show that $p'(x) = \frac{(1-\cos x)(k-h(x))}{h(x)}$.

b) Determine the range of $h(x)$ for $x \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

c) Find all real values of $k$ for which $p(x) \geq 0$ for all $x \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

positive_text: Find all functions $ g: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ such that $$ g\left(y + z^{2} + g(z)\right) = 2z + (g(y))^{2} $$ for all $ y, z \in \mathbb{R} $.

negatives.text: Find all functions $ f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ such that $$ f\left(x^{2}+y+f(y)\right)=2 y-(f(x))^{2} $$ for any $ x, y \in \mathbb{R} $.
Find all functions $ f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ such that $$ f\left(x^{2}+y+f(x)\right)=2 y+(f(x))^{2} $$ for any $ x, y \in \mathbb{R} $.
Find all functions $ f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ such that $$ f\left(x^{2}+y+f(y)\right)=2 y+(f(x)) $$ for any $ x, y \in \mathbb{R} $.

positive_text: Determine all real values of $ x $ for which $ 4[x m] = m + [x[x m]] $ holds for all positive integers $ m $ (with $ [y] $ representing the floor of $ y $).

negatives.text: Find all real numbers $ a $ such that $ 4[a n] = n + [a + [a n]] $ for all positive integers $ n $ (with $ [x] $ being the floor function).
Find all real numbers $ a $ such that $ 4[a n^2] = n + [a[a n]] $ for all positive integers $ n $ (where $ [x] $ denotes the floor of $ x $).

positive_text: Given any rearrangement $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{2002}$ of the numbers $1$ through $2002$, must there exist indices $i$ and $j$ with the same parity such that $1 \leq i < j \leq 2002$ and $b_{i} + b_{j} = 2 b_{\frac{i+j}{2}}$?

negatives.text: Is it true that for any permutation $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{2002}$ of $1,2, \ldots, 2002$ there are positive integers $m$ and $n$ of the same parity such that $1 \leq m < n \leq 2002$ and $a_{m} + a_{n} = a_{\frac{m+n}{2}}$?

Is it true that for any permutation $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{2002}$ of $1,2, \ldots, 2002$ there are positive integers $m$ and $n$ of the same parity such that $1 \leq m < n \leq 2002$ and $a_{m} + a_{n} = 2 a_{\frac{m+n}{2}} + 1$?

positive_text:
Find all real values of $k$, for which the equation
$$
\frac{2k}{(y+1)^{2}} + \frac{k+1}{y+1} - \frac{2(k+1)y - (k+3)}{2y^{2} - y - 1} = 0
$$
has two real roots $y_{1}$ and $y_{2}$ satisfying the condition $y_{2}^{2} - ky_{1} = k^{2} - k - 1$.

negatives.text:
Find all real values of $a$, for which the equation
$$
\frac{2a}{(x+1)^{2}} + \frac{a+1}{x+1} - \frac{2(a+1)x + (a+3)}{2x^{2} - x - 1} = 0
$$
has two real roots $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ satisfying the condition $x_{2}^{2} - ax_{1} = a^{2} - a - 1$.

Find all real values of $a$, for which the equation
$$
\frac{2a}{(x+1)^{2}} + \frac{a+1}{x+1} - \frac{2(a+1)x - (a+3)}{2x^{2} - x - 1} = 0
$$
has two real roots $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ satisfying the condition $x_{2}^{2} + ax_{1} = a^{2} - a - 1$.

Find all real values of $a$, for which the equation
$$
\frac{2a}{(x+1)^{2}} + \frac{a+1}{x+1} - \frac{2(a+1)x - (a+3)}{2x^{2} - x - 1} = 0
$$
has two real roots $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ satisfying the condition $x_{2}^{2} - ax_{1} = a^{2} - a + 1$.

positive_text: Let $PQRS$ be a parallelogram with $\angle QPS$ acute. Let $T$ and $U$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $S$ to $PQ$ and $PS$, respectively. A circle through $R$ and $U$ is tangent to diagonal $PR$ at a point $A$, and a circle through $Q$ and $T$ is tangent to the segment $AR$ at its midpoint $B$. Determine the length of diagonal $PR$ if $PA = 1$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with $\angle BAD$ acute. Let $E$ and $F$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $C$ to $AB$ and $AD$, respectively. A circle through $D$ and $F$ is tangent to the extension of $AC$ at a point $Q$, and a circle through $B$ and $E$ is tangent to segment $QC$ at its midpoint $P$. Find the length of diagonal $AC$ if $AQ = 1$.

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with $\angle BAD$ acute. Let $E$ and $F$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $C$ to $AB$ and $AD$, respectively. A circle through $D$ and $F$ is tangent to the diagonal $AC$ at a point $Q$, and a circle through $B$ and $E$ is tangent to segment $QC$ at its endpoint $P$. Find the length of diagonal $AC$ if $AQ = 1$.

positive_text: \text{Find the set of real values of } x \text{ such that } \sqrt{x^{2}-1}+\sqrt{2x^{2}-3}+\sqrt{3}x>0

negatives.text: \text{Solve the inequality } \sqrt{x^{2}-1}+\sqrt{2x^{2}+3}+x\sqrt{3}>0
\text{Solve the inequality } \sqrt{x^{2}+1}+\sqrt{2x^{2}-3}+x\sqrt{3}>0

positive_text:
Let $p(x) = x^{4} - x^{3} + 8k x^{2} - k x + k^{2}$ and $q(z) = z^{2} - z + 6k$.

a) Prove that $p(x) = \left(x^{2} - z_{1} x + k\right)\left(x^{2} - z_{2} x + k\right)$, where $z_{1}$ and $z_{2}$ are the roots of the equation $q(z) = 0$.

b) Determine all values of $k$ such that the equation $p(x) = 0$ has four distinct positive roots.

negatives.text:
Let $f(x) = x^{4} - x^{3} + 8a x^{2} + a x + a^{2}$ and $g(y) = y^{2} - y + 6a$.

a) Prove that $f(x) = \left(x^{2} - y_{1} x + a\right)\left(x^{2} - y_{2} x + a\right)$, where $y_{1}$ and $y_{2}$ are the roots of the equation $g(y) = 0$.

b) Find all values of $a$ such that the equation $f(x) = 0$ has four distinct positive roots.

Let $f(x) = x^{4} - x^{3} + 8a x^{2} - a x + a^{2}$ and $g(y) = y^{2} + y + 6a$.

a) Prove that $f(x) = \left(x^{2} - y_{1} x + a\right)\left(x^{2} - y_{2} x + a\right)$, where $y_{1}$ and $y_{2}$ are the roots of the equation $g(y) = 0$.

b) Find all values of $a$ such that the equation $f(x) = 0$ has four distinct positive roots.

Let $f(x) = x^{4} - x^{3} + 8a x^{2} - a x + a^{2}$ and $g(y) = y^{2} - y + 6a$.

a) Prove that $f(x) = \left(x^{2} - y_{1} x + a\right)\left(x^{2} - y_{2} x + a\right)$, where $y_{1}$ and $y_{2}$ are the roots of the equation $g(y) = 0$.

b) Find all values of $a$ such that the equation $f(x) = 0$ has four distinct positive real roots and at least one of them is irrational.

positive_text: A club has $b$ members who are boys and $g$ members who are girls, with $b \geq 1$, $1 \leq g < 2004$. Each member sends a greeting card to each other member. It is given that the total number of greeting cards sent by the boys equals the total number of greeting cards sent from one girl to another. Determine all possible values of $g$.

negatives.text: In a school there are $m$ boys and $j$ girls, $m \geq 1$, $1 \leq j < 2004$. Each student sends a post card to every other student, but not to themselves. It is known that the number of post cards sent by the boys is equal to the number of post cards sent by girls to boys. Find all possible values of $j$.

In a school there are $m$ boys and $j$ girls, $m \geq 1$, $1 \leq j < 2004$. Each student sends a post card to every student. It is known that the number of post cards sent by the boys is equal to the number of post cards sent from boys to girls. Find all possible values of $j$.

positive_text:
Let $g(x)$ be a cubic polynomial defined as
$$
g(x) = (k^{2} + 4k + 2)x^{3} + (k^{3} + 4k^{2} + k + 1)x^{2} + (2k - k^{2})x + k^{2},
$$
where $k$ is a real number.

a) Show that $g(-k) = 0$.

b) Determine all values of $k$ such that $g(x) = 0$ has three distinct positive real roots.

negatives.text:
Let $h(x)$ be the function
$$
h(x) = (b^{2} - 4b + 2)x^{3} + (b^{3} - 4b^{2} + b + 1)x^{2} + (2b - b^{2})x + b^{2},
$$
where $b$ is a real number.

a) Show that $h(-b) = 0$.

b) Find all values of $b$ such that $h(x) = 0$ has three distinct positive real roots.

Consider the cubic polynomial
$$
q(x) = (c^{2} + 4c + 2)x^{3} + (c^{3} + 4c^{2} + c + 1)x^{2} + (2c - c^{2})x + c^{3},
$$
where $c$ is a real number.

a) Prove that $q(-c) = 0$.

b) Find all values of $c$ such that $q(x) = 0$ has three distinct positive real roots.

Let $r(x)$ be defined as
$$
r(x) = (d^{2} + 4d + 2)x^{3} + (d^{3} + 4d^{2} + d + 1)x^{2} + (2d - d^{2})x + d^{2},
$$
where $d$ is a real number.

a) Show that $r(-d) = 0$.

b) Find all values of $d$ such that $r(x) = 0$ has three distinct negative real roots.

positive_text: Let $x, y, z \geq 1$ satisfy $x + y + z = 9$. Show that $$\sqrt{xy + yz + zx} \leq \sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y} + \sqrt{z}$$

negatives.text: Let $a, b, c \geq 1$ and $a + b + c = 9$. Prove that $$\sqrt{ab + bc + ca} \geq \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b} + \sqrt{c}$$
If $a, b, c \geq 1$ and $a + b + c = 10$, show that $$\sqrt{ab + bc + ca} \leq \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b} + \sqrt{c}$$

positive_text:
Determine all real values of $b$ such that the equation
$$
9^{x} - (b^{2} + 3b - 2) 3^{x} + 3b^{3} - 2b^{2} = 0
$$
has exactly one solution.

negatives.text:
Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
4^{x} + (a^{2} + 3a - 2) 2^{x} + 3a^{3} - 2a^{2} = 0
$$
has a unique solution.

Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
4^{2x} - (a^{2} + 3a - 2) 2^{x} + 3a^{3} - 2a^{2} = 0
$$
has a unique solution.

Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
4^{x} - (a^{2} + 3a - 2) 2^{x} + 3a^{3} + 2a^{2} = 0
$$
has a unique solution.

positive_text:
Determine all real values of $ a $ for which the equation
$$
\log_{4 a y}(y - 3 a) + \frac{1}{2} \log_{y - 3 a}(4 a y) = \frac{3}{2}
$$
has precisely two real solutions $ y $.

negatives.text:
Find all real numbers $ a $ such that the equation
$$
\log_{4 a x}(x - 3 a) - \frac{1}{2} \log_{x - 3 a}(4 a x) = \frac{3}{2}
$$
has exactly two real solutions.

Find all real numbers $ a $ such that the equation
$$
\log_{4 a x}(x - 3 a) + \frac{1}{2} \log_{x - 3 a}(4 a x) = -\frac{3}{2}
$$
has exactly two real solutions.

Find all real numbers $ a $ such that the equation
$$
\log_{4 a x}(x - 3 a) + \log_{x - 3 a}(4 a x) = \frac{3}{2}
$$
has exactly two real solutions.

positive_text: Let $ k \geq 3 $ and $ t \geq 2 $ be integers. Show that in a set of $ P = k t - t + 1 $ individuals where every subset of size $ k $ contains at least one pair of acquaintances, there exists an individual who knows at least $ t $ others. Is the result still valid if $ P < k t - t + 1 $?

negatives.text: Let $ m \geq 3 $ and $ n \geq 2 $ be integers. Prove that in a group of $ N = m n - n $ people such that there are two familiar people among any $ m $, there is a person who is familiar with $ n $ people. Does the statement remain true if $ N < m n - n $?

Let $ m \geq 3 $ and $ n \geq 2 $ be integers. Prove that in a group of $ N = m n - n + 1 $ people such that there is at least one pair of familiar people in any subset of size $ m $, there are at least two people who are familiar with $ n $ people. Does the statement remain true if $ N < m n - n + 1 $?

positive_text: Let $k$ be an integer, $1 < k < 100$. For every rearrangement $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{100}$ of the numbers $1$ through $100$, define $b_{101} = 0$. Determine the smallest index $m > k$ such that $b_{m}$ is smaller than at least $k-1$ of the numbers $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{k}$. Find all values of $k$ such that the number of rearrangements with $b_{m} = 1$ is equal to $\frac{100!}{4}$.

negatives.text: Let $k$ be an integer, $1 < k < 100$. For every permutation $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{100}$ of the integers $1$ through $100$, set $a_{101} = 101$. Determine the smallest index $m > k$ such that $a_{m}$ is less than at least $k-1$ of the numbers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{k}$. Find all $k$ for which the number of permutations with $a_{m} = 1$ is equal to $\frac{100!}{4}$.

Let $k$ be an integer, $1 < k < 100$. For every permutation $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{100}$ of the integers $1$ through $100$, set $a_{101} = 0$. Determine the smallest index $m > k$ such that $a_{m}$ is less than at least $k$ of the numbers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{k}$. Find all $k$ for which the number of permutations with $a_{m} = 1$ is equal to $\frac{100!}{4}$.

Let $k$ be an integer, $1 < k < 100$. For every permutation $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{100}$ of the integers $1$ through $100$, set $a_{101} = 0$. Determine the smallest index $m > k$ such that $a_{m}$ is less than at least $k-1$ of the numbers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{k}$. Find all $k$ for which the number of permutations with $a_{m} = 2$ is equal to $\frac{100!}{4}$.

positive_text: Find all integer solutions $ (x, y, z) $ to the equation $ 8 y^{2} + 2^{x} - 3^{z} = 283 $.

negatives.text: Solve in integers the equation $ 2^{a} + 8 b^{2} + 3^{c} = 283 $.
Solve in integers the equation $ 2^{a} + 8 b^{2} - 3^{c} = 284 $.
Solve in integers the equation $ 2^{a} + 8 b^{3} - 3^{c} = 283 $.

positive_text: \text{Let } b_{1} > 0 \text{ and } b_{n+1} = b_{n} + \frac{n}{b_{n}} \text{ for } n \geq 1. \text{ Prove that:}\\\text{a)}\ b_{n} \geq n \text{ for } n \geq 2;\\\text{b)}\ \text{the sequence } \left\{\frac{b_{n}}{n}\right\}_{n \geq 1} \text{ converges and find its limit.}

negatives.text: \text{Let } a_{1} > 0 \text{ and } a_{n+1} = a_{n} + \frac{n+1}{a_{n}} \text{ for } n \geq 1. \text{ Prove that:}\\\text{a)}\ a_{n} \geq n \text{ for } n \geq 2;\\\text{b)}\ \text{the sequence } \left\{\frac{a_{n}}{n}\right\}_{n \geq 1} \text{ converges and find its limit.}

\text{Let } a_{1} > 0 \text{ and } a_{n+1} = a_{n} + \frac{\sqrt{n}}{a_{n}} \text{ for } n \geq 1. \text{ Prove that:}\\\text{a)}\ a_{n} \geq n \text{ for } n \geq 2;\\\text{b)}\ \text{the sequence } \left\{\frac{a_{n}}{n}\right\}_{n \geq 1} \text{ converges and find its limit.}

\text{Let } a_{1} > 0 \text{ and } a_{n+1} = a_{n} + \frac{n}{a_{n}^2} \text{ for } n \geq 1. \text{ Prove that:}\\\text{a)}\ a_{n} \geq n \text{ for } n \geq 2;\\\text{b)}\ \text{the sequence } \left\{\frac{a_{n}}{n}\right\}_{n \geq 1} \text{ converges and find its limit.}

positive_text: Determine all values of $b$ such that the maximum value of $g(x) = \frac{b x - 1}{x^{4} - x^{2} + 1}$ is exactly $1$.

negatives.text: Find all values of $a$ such that the minimum of the function $f(x) = \frac{a x - 1}{x^{4} - x^{2} + 1}$ is equal to $1$.
Find all values of $a$ such that the maximum of the function $f(x) = \frac{a x^{2} - 1}{x^{4} - x^{2} + 1}$ is equal to $1$.
Find all values of $a$ such that the maximum of the function $f(x) = \frac{a x - 1}{x^{4} - x^{2} + 1}$ is greater than $1$.

positive_text: Let $k$ be an integer with $k \geq 4$. Show that there are infinitely many squarefree integers $m$ such that $m$ divides $k^m - 1$.

negatives.text: Prove that for any integer $b \geq 4$ there exist infinitely many squarefree positive integers $n$ that divide $b^{n} + 1$.
Prove that for any integer $c \geq 4$ there exist infinitely many squarefree positive integers $n$ that divide $c^{n} - 2$.
Prove that for any integer $d \geq 4$ there exist infinitely many squarefree positive integers $n$ such that $d - 1$ divides $n$.

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with an incircle. Given that $AC = BC$, $AD = 5$, the diagonals intersect at point $F$, and $BF = 12$, $DF = 3$, determine $\angle BCD$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a circumscribed quadrilateral with $AC = BC$, $AD = 5$, and diagonals intersecting at point $E$ such that $BE = 12$ and $ED = 3$. Find $\angle CBD$.
Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with $AC = BC$, $AD = 5$, and diagonals intersecting at point $E$ such that $BE = 12$ and $DE = 3$. Find $\angle BCD$.

positive_text:
a) A set $S$ of positive integers less than $2000000$ is called special if $2000 \in S$ and for any $x, y \in S$ with $x < y$, $x$ divides $y$. Determine the largest possible size of a special set.

b) How many special sets of maximum size exist?

negatives.text:
a) A set $A$ of positive integers less than $2000000$ is called good if $2000 \in A$ and $a + b$ is divisible by $a$ for any $a, b \in A$, $a < b$. Find the maximum possible cardinality of a good set.

b) Find the number of the good sets of maximal cardinality.

a) A set $A$ of positive integers less than $2000000$ is called good if $2000 \in A$ and $a^2$ divides $b^2$ for any $a, b \in A$, $a < b$. Find the maximum possible cardinality of a good set.

b) Find the number of the good sets of maximal cardinality.

positive_text: Determine all non-constant polynomials $A(x)$ and $B(x)$ with real coefficients satisfying $A(x) B(x+1) = A(x+2004) B(x)$ for all real $x$.

negatives.text: Find all non-constant polynomials $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ with real coefficients such that $P(x) Q(x+1) = P(x+2003) Q(x)$ for all $x$.
Find all non-constant polynomials $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ with real coefficients such that $P(x+1) Q(x+1) = P(x+2004) Q(x)$ for all $x$.
Find all non-constant polynomials $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ with real coefficients such that $P(x) Q(x+1) = P(x+2004) Q(x+1)$ for all $x$.

positive_text: Let $S = \{a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n\}$, $n \geq 4$. For any function $g: S \rightarrow S$ and any $x \in S$, define $g^{(1)}(x) = g(x)$, $g^{(k+1)}(x) = g(g^{(k)}(x))$, $k \geq 1$. How many functions $g$ are there such that $g^{(n-2)}$ is constant but $g^{(n-3)}$ is not?

negatives.text: Let $A = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, $n \geq 4$. For any function $f: A \rightarrow A$ and any $a \in A$, define $f_{1}(a) = f(a)$, $f_{i+1}(a) = f(f_{i}(a))$, $i \geq 1$. Find the number of functions $f$ such that $f_{n-1}$ is constant but $f_{n-2}$ is not.

Let $A = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, $n \geq 4$. For any function $f: A \rightarrow A$ and any $a \in A$, define $f_{1}(a) = f(a)$, $f_{i+1}(a) = f(f_{i}(a))$, $i \geq 1$. Find the number of functions $f$ such that $f_{n-2}$ is constant and $f_{n-3}$ is also constant.

Let $A = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, $n \geq 4$. For any function $f: A \rightarrow A$ and any $a \in A$, define $f_{1}(a) = f(a)$, $f_{i+1}(a) = f(f_{i}(a))$, $i \geq 1$. Find the number of functions $f$ such that $f_{n-2}$ is injective but $f_{n-3}$ is not.

positive_text: Suppose $A(x)$ and $B(x)$ are polynomials each having at least 2 non-vanishing terms. If $\frac{A(x)}{B(x)}$ is not constant, determine the minimal number of non-zero terms that the bivariate polynomial $g(s, t) = A(s)B(t) - A(t)B(s)$ can have.

negatives.text: Let $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ be polynomials with $m \geq 2$ non-zero coefficients. If $\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$ is not a constant function, find the least possible number of the non-zero coefficients of the polynomial $f(u, v)=p(u) q(v)+p(v) q(u)$.

Let $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ be polynomials with $m \geq 2$ non-zero coefficients. If $\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$ is not a constant function, find the least possible number of the non-zero coefficients of the polynomial $f(u, v)=p(u) q(v)-p(v) q(u)^2$.

positive_text: Let $S$ and $T$ lie on the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of quadrilateral $ABCD$ such that $\frac{AS}{AC} + \frac{BT}{BD} = 1$. The segment $ST$ intersects $AD$ at $X$ and $BC$ at $Y$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $AXS$, $BYT$, $DXS$, and $CYS$ are concurrent.

negatives.text: Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of quadrilateral $ABCD$ such that $\frac{AP}{AC} + \frac{BQ}{BD} = 2$. The line $PQ$ meets $AD$ and $BC$ at $M$ and $N$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $AMP$, $BNQ$, $DMQ$, and $CNP$ are concurrent.

Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on the sides $AB$ and $CD$ of quadrilateral $ABCD$ such that $\frac{AP}{AB} + \frac{CQ}{CD} = 1$. The segment $PQ$ meets $AD$ and $BC$ at $M$ and $N$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $AMP$, $BNQ$, $DMQ$, and $CNP$ are concurrent.

Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of quadrilateral $ABCD$ such that $\frac{AP}{AC} + \frac{BQ}{BD} = 1$. The segment $PQ$ meets $AB$ and $CD$ at $M$ and $N$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $AMP$, $BNQ$, $DMQ$, and $CNP$ are concurrent.

positive_text: Let $p$, $q$ and $m$ be positive integers. Define $R(m)$ to be the number of ways to express $1$ as a sum of $m$ unit fractions. Let $S(c, d)$ be the smallest positive integer $n$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{y_i} = \frac{c}{d}$ has a solution in positive integers and let $S(d) = \max\{S(c, d) : 1 \leq c \leq d\}$. Show that the number of positive divisors of $d$ is at most $2 S(d) + R(S(d) + 2)$.

negatives.text: Let $a$, $b$ and $n$ be positive integers. Define $K(n)$ to be the number of ways to express $1$ as a sum of $n$ unit fractions. Let $L(a, b)$ be the smallest positive integer $m$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{m} \frac{1}{x_i} = \frac{a}{b}$ has a solution in positive integers and set $L(b) = \min\{L(a, b) : 1 \leq a \leq b\}$. Prove that the number of positive divisors of $b$ is at most $2 L(b) + K(L(b) + 2)$.

Let $a$, $b$ and $n$ be positive integers. Define $K(n)$ as the number of ways to express $1$ as a product of $n$ unit fractions. Let $L(a, b)$ be the least positive integer $m$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{m} \frac{1}{x_i} = \frac{a}{b}$ has a solution in positive integers and set $L(b) = \max\{L(a, b) : 1 \leq a \leq b\}$. Prove that the number of positive divisors of $b$ is at most $2 L(b) + K(L(b) + 2)$.

Let $a$, $b$ and $n$ be positive integers. Define $K(n)$ to be the number of representations of $\frac{1}{2}$ as a sum of $n$ unit fractions. Let $L(a, b)$ be the least positive integer $m$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{m} \frac{1}{x_i} = \frac{a}{b}$ has a solution in positive integers and set $L(b) = \max\{L(a, b) : 1 \leq a \leq b\}$. Prove that the number of positive divisors of $b$ is at most $2 L(b) + K(L(b) + 2)$.

positive_text: Let $G$ be a graph with $2n$ vertices, $n \geq 4$. Each edge is colored either blue or red. It is given that the blue subgraph contains no triangles and the red subgraph contains no $K_n$. Determine the minimum number of blue edges.

negatives.text: The edges of a graph with $2n$ vertices, $n \geq 4$, are colored in blue and red such that there is no blue triangle and there is no red cycle of length $n$. Find the least possible number of the blue edges.

The edges of a graph with $2n$ vertices, $n \geq 4$, are colored in blue and red such that there is no red triangle and there is no blue complete subgraph with $n$ vertices. Find the least possible number of the blue edges.

The edges of a graph with $2n$ vertices, $n \geq 4$, are colored in blue and red such that there is no blue triangle and there is no red complete subgraph with $n$ edges. Find the least possible number of the blue edges.

positive_text: The internal angle bisectors of $\angle X$, $\angle Y$ and $\angle Z$ in triangle $\triangle XYZ$ intersect the circumcircle of $\triangle XYZ$ at points $X_1$, $Y_1$, and $Z_1$, respectively. Let $XX_1 \cap ZZ_1 = J$, $XX_1 \cap YZ = R$, and $YY_1 \cap X_1Z_1 = Q$. Let $K$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle JZ_1Q$ and suppose $KQ \cap YZ = S$ with $YS = SR$. Given that $\angle YXZ = 2\angle XYZ$, determine the angles of $\triangle XYZ$.

negatives.text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with angle bisectors of $\angle A$, $\angle B$, and $\angle C$ meeting the circumcircle at $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$, respectively. Define $AA_1 \cap CC_1 = I$, $AA_1 \cap BC = N$, and $BB_1 \cap A_1C_1 = P$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle IPC_1$, and suppose $OP \cap BC = M$. If $BM = MN$ and $\angle BAC = 2 \angle ACB$, find the angles of $\triangle ABC$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with internal angle bisectors of $\angle A$, $\angle B$, and $\angle C$ meeting the circumcircle at $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$, respectively. Set $AA_1 \cap CC_1 = I$, $AA_1 \cap BC = N$, and $BB_1 \cap A_1C_1 = P$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle IPC_1$, and suppose $OP \cap BC = M$. If $BM = 2MN$ and $\angle BAC = 2 \angle ABC$, find the angles of $\triangle ABC$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with angle bisectors of $\angle A$, $\angle B$, and $\angle C$ meeting the circumcircle at $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$, respectively. Set $AA_1 \cap CC_1 = I$, $AA_1 \cap BC = N$, and $BB_1 \cap A_1C_1 = P$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle IPC_1$, and suppose $OP \cap BC = M$. If $BM = MN$ and $\angle ABC = 2 \angle BAC$, find the angles of $\triangle ABC$.

positive_text:
Determine all real numbers $a$ for which the quadratic equation
$$
((a - 2)^2 - a - 7) x^{2} - 6x - a = 0
$$
has two distinct solutions that are both positive.

negatives.text:
Find all real values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
(a^{2}+a-9) x^{2} - 6x - a = 0
$$
has two distinct positive roots.

Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
(a^{2}-a-9) x^{2} - 6x + a = 0
$$
has two distinct positive roots.

Find all values of $a$ such that the equation
$$
(a^{2}-a-9) x^{2} - 6x - a = 0
$$
has two distinct negative roots.

positive_text: \text{Find all values of } b \text{ such that the equation } \sqrt{(4b^2 - 4b - 1)y^2 - 2by + 1} = 1 - by - y^2 \text{ has exactly two solutions.}

negatives.text: \text{Find all values of } a \text{ such that the equation } \sqrt{(4a^2 - 4a - 1)x^2 - 2ax + 1} = 1 + ax - x^2 \text{ has exactly two solutions.}
\text{Find all values of } a \text{ such that the equation } \sqrt{(4a^2 - 4a - 1)x^2 - 2ax + 1} = 1 - ax - x^2 \text{ has exactly three solutions.}

positive_text: In triangle $ABC$, let $I$ be the incenter and $M$ the midpoint of segment $AB$. Suppose $CI = IM$. Determine the smallest possible measure of angle $\angle CIM$.

negatives.text: Let $I$ be the incenter of $\triangle ABC$ and $M$ be the midpoint of the side $AB$. Suppose $CI = IM$. Find the largest possible value of $\angle CIM$.
Let $I$ be the incenter of $\triangle ABC$ and $M$ be the midpoint of the side $BC$. Suppose $CI = IM$. Find the least possible value of $\angle CIM$.
Let $I$ be the incenter of $\triangle ABC$ and $M$ be the midpoint of the side $AB$. Suppose $IM = BI$. Find the least possible value of $\angle CIM$.

positive_text: In $\triangle XYZ$ with $XY = XZ$, let $P$ and $Q$ lie on $XZ$ and $YZ$, respectively, such that $4 XP \cdot YQ = XY^2$. Prove that the line $XY$ and the angle bisectors of $\angle XPQ$ and $\angle YQP$ are concurrent.

negatives.text: Let $A_1$ and $B_1$ be points on the sides $AC$ and $BC$ of $\triangle ABC$ such that $4 AA_1^2 + BB_1^2 = AB^2$. If $AC = BC$, prove that the line $AB$ and the bisectors of $\angle AA_1B_1$ and $\angle BB_1A_1$ are concurrent.

Let $A_1$ and $B_1$ be points on the sides $AC$ and $BC$ of $\triangle ABC$ such that $4 AA_1 \cdot BB_1 = AB^2$. If $AC = 2BC$, prove that the line $AB$ and the bisectors of $\angle AA_1B_1$ and $\angle BB_1A_1$ are concurrent.

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with center $O$, and suppose its diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $F$. If the midpoints of $AD$, $BC$, and $OF$ lie on a straight line, show that $AB = CD$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with center $I$, and suppose diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $E$. If the midpoints of $AB$, $CD$, and $IE$ are collinear, prove that $AD = BC$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with center $I$, and suppose diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $E$. If the midpoints of $AD$, $BC$, and $IE$ are collinear, prove that $ABCD$ is a rectangle.

positive_text:
Let $x, y, z > 0$ with $x + y + z = 1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{9}{10} \leq \frac{x}{1 + yz} + \frac{y}{1 + zx} + \frac{z}{1 + xy} < 1
$$

negatives.text:
Let $a, b, c > 0$ with $a + b + c = 1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{2} \leq \frac{a}{1 + b + c} + \frac{b}{1 + c + a} + \frac{c}{1 + a + b} < 1
$$

Let $a, b, c > 0$ such that $a + b + c = 1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{9}{10} \leq \frac{a}{1 + b^2 c^2} + \frac{b}{1 + c^2 a^2} + \frac{c}{1 + a^2 b^2} < 1
$$

Let $a, b, c > 0$ with $abc = 1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{9}{10} \leq \frac{a}{1 + bc} + \frac{b}{1 + ca} + \frac{c}{1 + ab} < 1
$$

positive_text: \text{Find all integer solutions to the equation} \quad a^{3} + 10a - 1 = b^{3} + 6b^{2}

negatives.text: \text{Solve in integers the equation} \quad x^{3} + 10x + 1 = y^{3} + 6y^{2}
\text{Solve in integers the equation} \quad x^{3} + 10x^{2} - 1 = y^{3} + 6y^{2}
\text{Solve in integers the equation} \quad x^{3} + 10x - 1 = y^{3} + 6y^{3}

positive_text: A grid of size $n \times n$ ($n \geq 2$) has each cell colored either black or white. The coloring must satisfy the condition that for every rectangle with at least four cells, the colors at its four corners are not all the same. Determine the largest possible value of $n$.

negatives.text: A square $n \times n$ ($n \geq 2$) is divided into $n^2$ unit squares colored in black or white such that the squares at the four corners of any rectangle (containing at least four squares) have all the same color. Find the maximum possible value of $n$.

positive_text:
Let $PQR$ be an acute triangle. Determine the set of points $N$ inside $\triangle PQR$ for which
$$
PR - ST = \frac{NS \cdot RT + NT \cdot SP}{QN}
$$
where $S$ and $T$ are the feet of the perpendiculars from $N$ to the lines $QR$ and $PR$, respectively.

negatives.text:
Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Find the locus of the points $M$ in the interior of $\triangle ABC$ such that
$$
AB + FG = \frac{MF \cdot AG + MG \cdot BF}{CM}
$$
where $F$ and $G$ are the feet of the perpendiculars from $M$ to the lines $BC$ and $AC$, respectively.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Determine the set of points $M$ in the interior of $\triangle ABC$ such that
$$
AB - FG = \frac{MF^2 + MG^2}{CM}
$$
where $F$ and $G$ are the feet of the perpendiculars from $M$ to the lines $BC$ and $AC$, respectively.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Find the locus of the points $M$ in the interior of $\triangle ABC$ such that
$$
AB - FG = \frac{MF \cdot AG + MG \cdot BF}{AM}
$$
where $F$ and $G$ are the feet of the perpendiculars from $M$ to the lines $BC$ and $AC$, respectively.

positive_text:
Given the inequality $|x^{2}-5x+6| \leq x + k$, where $k$ is a real number.

a) Determine the solution set when $k = 0$.

b) Find the values of $k$ for which the inequality has exactly three integer solutions.

negatives.text:
Consider the inequality $|x^{2}-5x+6| < x + a$, where $a$ is a real parameter.

a) Solve the inequality for $a=0$.

b) Find the values of $a$ for which the inequality has exactly three integer solutions.

Consider the inequality $|x^{2}-5x+6| \leq x^{2} + a$, where $a$ is a real parameter.

a) Solve the inequality for $a=0$.

b) Find the values of $a$ for which the inequality has exactly three integer solutions.

Consider the inequality $|x^{2}-5x+6| \leq x + a$, where $a$ is a real parameter.

a) Solve the inequality for $a=0$.

b) Find the values of $a$ for which the inequality has exactly three positive integer solutions.

negatives.text: \text{Solve the equation } (x+6) 5^{1-|x-1|}-x=(x+1)\left|5^{-x}-1\right|+5^{x+1}+1
\text{Solve the equation } (x+6) 5^{1-|x-1|}-x=(x+1)\left|5^{x}-1\right|+5^{x+1}-1
\text{Solve the equation } (x+6) 5^{1-|x-1|}-x=(x+1)\left|5^{x}-1\right|+5^{x+1}+1, \text{ for } x > 0

positive_text: Let triangle $XYZ$ have an altitude $ZT$ with $T$ lying on side $XY$. Let $M$ and $N$ be the incenters of $\triangle XZT$ and $\triangle YZT$, respectively. Prove that quadrilateral $XYNM$ is cyclic if and only if either $XZ = YZ$ or $\angle XZY = 90^\circ$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with altitude $CH$, where $H$ is an interior point of the side $AB$. Denote by $P$ and $Q$ the incenters of $\triangle AHC$ and $\triangle BHC$, respectively. Prove that the quadrilateral $ABQP$ is cyclic if and only if either $AC = AB$ or $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with altitude $CH$, where $H$ is an interior point of the side $AB$. Denote by $P$ and $Q$ the incenters of $\triangle AHC$ and $\triangle BHC$, respectively. Prove that the quadrilateral $ABQP$ is cyclic if and only if either $AC = BC$ or $\angle ACB = 120^\circ$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with altitude $CH$, where $H$ is an interior point of the side $AB$. Denote by $P$ and $Q$ the incenters of $\triangle AHC$ and $\triangle BHC$, respectively. Prove that the quadrilateral $ABQP$ is cyclic if and only if either $AC = BC$ or $\angle ACB$ is a right angle, and $H$ lies outside segment $AB$.

positive_text: Find all integer solutions $ (a, b, c) $ such that $$ c^{2}+1=ab(ab+2b-2a-4). $$

negatives.text: Solve in integers the equation $$ z^{2}+1=xy(xy+2y+2x-4). $$
Solve in integers the equation $$ z^{2}-1=xy(xy+2y-2x-4). $$
Solve in integers the equation $$ z^{2}+1=xy(xy+2y-2x-4)^2. $$

positive_text:
On an $n \times n$ board with $n \geq 2$, each cell contains either $+1$ or $-1$. Define the neighbors of a cell $(i, j)$ as the four adjacent cells in the toroidal grid (i.e., with wrap-around). In each step, update the value of each cell to be the product of its four neighbors. For instance, if the board is

\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
+1 & -1 & +1 \\
\hline
+1 & -1 & -1 \\
\hline
-1 & +1 & -1 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\quad $\rightarrow$ \quad
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
+1 & -1 & -1 \\
\hline
-1 & +1 & +1 \\
\hline
-1 & +1 & +1 \\
\hline
\end{tabular},

then the next configuration is shown. A board is called "achievable" if it can be turned into the all-$+1$ configuration in finitely many steps. Determine all $n$ for which every $n \times n$ board is achievable.

negatives.text: On an $n \times n$ board with $n \geq 2$, each cell contains either $+1$ or $-1$. The neighbors of a cell $(i, j)$ are the four adjacent cells, with wrap-around allowed. In each step, update the value of each cell to be the sum of its four neighbors. A board is called "achievable" if it can be turned into the all-$+1$ configuration in finitely many steps. Determine all $n$ for which every $n \times n$ board is achievable.

On an $n \times n$ board with $n \geq 2$, each cell contains either $+1$ or $-1$. The neighbors of a cell $(i, j)$ are the four adjacent cells, with wrap-around allowed. In each step, update the value of each cell to be the product of its three neighbors, excluding one fixed direction (e.g., the cell above). A board is called "achievable" if it can be turned into the all-$+1$ configuration in finitely many steps. Determine all $n$ for which every $n \times n$ board is achievable.

On an $n \times n$ board with $n \geq 2$, each cell contains either $+1$ or $-1$. The neighbors of a cell $(i, j)$ are the four adjacent cells, with wrap-around allowed. In each step, update the value of each cell to be the product of its four neighbors, but only if the current value is $-1$; otherwise, the value remains unchanged. A board is called "achievable" if it can be turned into the all-$+1$ configuration in finitely many steps. Determine all $n$ for which every $n \times n$ board is achievable.

positive_text:
Find all real values of the parameter $k$ for which the number of real solutions of the equation
$$
3\left(5 x^{2}-k^{4}\right)-2 x=2 k^{2}(6 x-1)
$$
is not greater than the number of real solutions of the equation
$$
2 x^{3}+6 x=\left(3^{6 k}-9\right) \sqrt{2^{8 k}-\frac{1}{6}}-(3 k-1)^{2} 12^{x}
$$

negatives.text:
Find all real values of the parameter $a$ for which the number of real solutions of the equation
$$
3\left(5 x^{2}-a^{4}\right)+2 x=2 a^{2}(6 x-1)
$$
is not greater than the number of real solutions of the equation
$$
2 x^{3}+6 x=\left(3^{6 a}-9\right) \sqrt{2^{8 a}-\frac{1}{6}}-(3 a-1)^{2} 12^{x}
$$

Find all real values of the parameter $a$ for which the number of real solutions of the equation
$$
3\left(5 x^{2}-a^{4}\right)-2 x=2 a^{2}(6 x-1)
$$
is not greater than the number of real solutions of the equation
$$
2 x^{3}+6 x=\left(3^{6 a}-9\right) \sqrt{2^{8 a}-\frac{1}{6}}-(3 a-1)^{2} 12^{-x}
$$

Find all real values of the parameter $a$ for which the number of real solutions of the equation
$$
3\left(5 x^{2}-a^{4}\right)-2 x=2 a^{2}(6 x-1)
$$
is not greater than the number of real solutions of the equation
$$
2 x^{3}+6 x=\left(3^{6 a}-9\right) \sqrt{2^{8 a}-\frac{1}{6}}-(3 a-1)^{2} 12^{x} + 1
$$

positive_text:
A sequence $\{b_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is defined by $b_{1} = 0$ and $b_{n+1} = b_{n} + 4n + 3$, $n \geq 1$.

a) Find a closed-form expression for $b_{n}$.

b) Evaluate the limit
$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\sqrt{b_{n}} + \sqrt{b_{4n}} + \sqrt{b_{4^{2}n}} + \cdots + \sqrt{b_{4^{10}n}}}{\sqrt{b_{n}} + \sqrt{b_{2n}} + \sqrt{b_{2^{2}n}} + \cdots + \sqrt{b_{2^{10}n}}}
$$

negatives.text:
Let $\{d_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence defined by $d_{1} = 0$ and $d_{n+1} = d_{n} + 4n + 3$, $n \geq 1$.

a) Find a formula for $d_{n}$.

b) Evaluate the limit
$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\sqrt{d_{n}} + \sqrt{d_{4n}} + \sqrt{d_{4^{2}n}} + \cdots + \sqrt{d_{4^{10}n}}}{\sqrt{d_{n}} + \sqrt{d_{3n}} + \sqrt{d_{3^{2}n}} + \cdots + \sqrt{d_{3^{10}n}}}
$$

positive_text:
Solve the inequality
$$
\log_{k}\left(t^{2}-t-2\right) > \log_{k}\left(3+2t-t^{2}\right)
$$
if it is known that $t=k+1$ is a solution.

negatives.text:
Solve the inequality
$$
\log_{a}\left(x^{2}-x-2\right) < \log_{a}\left(3+2x-x^{2}\right)
$$
if it is known that $x=a+1$ is a solution.

Solve the inequality
$$
\log_{a}\left(x^{2}-x-2\right) > \log_{a}\left(3+2x+x^{2}\right)
$$
if it is known that $x=a+1$ is a solution.

Solve the inequality
$$
\log_{a}\left(x^{2}-x-2\right) > \log_{a}\left(3+2x-x^{2}\right)
$$
if it is known that $x=a$ is a solution.

positive_text: \text{Find all real values of } a \text{ such that the equation} \quad \log_{10} (a x + 1) = \log_{10} (x - 1) + \log_{10} (2 - x) \quad \text{has a unique solution}.

negatives.text: \text{Find all real values of } a \text{ such that the equation} \quad \lg (a x + 1) = \lg (x - 1) - \lg (2 - x) \quad \text{has exactly one real solution}.
\text{Find all real values of } a \text{ such that the equation} \quad \lg (a x + 1) = \lg (x - 1) + \lg (x - 2) \quad \text{has exactly one real solution}.
\text{Find all real values of } a \text{ such that the equation} \quad \lg (a x^2 + 1) = \lg (x - 1) + \lg (2 - x) \quad \text{has exactly one real solution}.

positive_text:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be acute with area $1$. On side $BC$, point $A_1$ is selected so that $\angle AA_1C = \varphi$; on side $CA$, point $B_1$ is selected so that $\angle BB_1A = \varphi$; and on side $AB$, point $C_1$ is selected so that $\angle CC_1B = \varphi$, where $\varphi$ is acute. Let $AA_1$, $BB_1$, and $CC_1$ intersect at points $M$, $N$, and $P$ respectively.

a) Show that the circumcenter of triangle $MNP$ is the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$.

b) Determine $\varphi$ if the area of triangle $MNP$ is $2 - \sqrt{3}$.

negatives.text:
In an acute triangle $\triangle ABC$ of area $1$, points $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$ lie on sides $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ respectively such that $\angle CC_1B = \angle AA_1C = \angle BB_1A = \varphi$, where $\varphi$ is acute. The lines $A_1B_1$, $B_1C_1$, and $C_1A_1$ intersect at points $M$, $N$, and $P$.

a) Prove that the circumcenter of triangle $MNP$ coincides with the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$.

b) Find $\varphi$ if the area of triangle $MNP$ is $2 - \sqrt{3}$.

In an acute triangle $\triangle ABC$ of area $1$, points $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$ lie on sides $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ respectively such that $\angle CC_1B = \angle AA_1C = \angle BB_1A = \varphi$, where $\varphi$ is acute. The cevians $AA_1$, $BB_1$, and $CC_1$ intersect at point $O$.

a) Prove that the circumcenter of triangle $MNP$ coincides with the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$.

b) Find $\varphi$ if the area of triangle $MNP$ is $2 - \sqrt{3}$.

positive_text:
Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer. The positive integers $x$, $y$, $z$ and $w$ are less than or equal to $n$, $w$ is the largest one and they satisfy the equality
$$
(xy + wz)(yz + xw)(xz + yw) = (w - x)^2 (w - y)^2 (w - z)^2
$$

a) Prove that $w = x + y + z$.

b) Find the number of the quadruples $(x, y, z, w)$ which have the required properties.

negatives.text:
Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer. The positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ are less than or equal to $n$, $d$ is the largest one and they satisfy the inequality
$$
(ab + cd)(bc + ad)(ac + bd) < (d - a)^2 (d - b)^2 (d - c)^2
$$

a) Prove that $d = a + b + c$.

b) Find the number of the quadruples $(a, b, c, d)$ which have the required properties.

Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer. The positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ are less than or equal to $n$, $d$ is the largest one and they satisfy the equality
$$
(ab + cd)(bc + ad)(ac + bd) = (d^2 - a^2)(d^2 - b^2)(d^2 - c^2)
$$

a) Prove that $d = a + b + c$.

b) Find the number of the quadruples $(a, b, c, d)$ which have the required properties.

Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer. The positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ are less than or equal to $n$, $d$ is the largest one and they satisfy the equality
$$
(ab + cd)(bc + ad)(ac + bd) = (d - a)(d - b)(d - c)
$$

a) Prove that $d = a + b + c$.

b) Find the number of the quadruples $(a, b, c, d)$ which have the required properties.

positive_text: Let $d$ be a positive integer and let $\{b_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of positive integers satisfying $b_{n} < b_{n+1} < b_{n} + d$ for all $n \geq 1$. Concatenate the digits of the sequence to form an infinite string. Show that for any positive integer $n$, there exists a positive integer $k$ such that the number formed by the first $k$ digits is divisible by $n$.

negatives.text: Let $c$ be a positive integer and let $\{a_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of positive integers such that $a_{n+1} > a_{n} + c$ for every $n \geq 1$. The terms are written in order to form an infinite sequence of digits. Prove that for every positive integer $m$ there exists a positive integer $k$ such that the number formed by the first $k$ digits is divisible by $m$.

Let $c$ be a positive integer and let $\{a_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of positive integers such that $a_{n} < a_{n+1} < a_{n} + c$ for every $n \geq 1$. The terms are written in reverse order (from $a_{\infty}$ to $a_1$) to form an infinite sequence of digits. Prove that for every positive integer $m$ there exists a positive integer $k$ such that the number formed by the first $k$ digits is divisible by $m$.

Let $c$ be a positive integer and let $\{a_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of positive integers such that $a_{n} < a_{n+1} < a_{n} + c$ for every $n \geq 1$. The terms are written in base 2 instead of base 10 to form an infinite sequence of digits. Prove that for every positive integer $m$ there exists a positive integer $k$ such that the number formed by the first $k$ digits is divisible by $m$.

positive_text:
Let triangle $PQR$ be isosceles with $PQ = PR = 1$ and base $QR = 2a$, where $a > 0$.

a) Find the inradius $r$ of $\triangle PQR$ in terms of $a$.

b) Determine the maximum value of $r$.

negatives.text:
Let triangle $ABC$ have sides $AB = AC = 1$ and base $BC = 2x$, where $x > 0$.

a) Find the circumradius $R$ of $\triangle ABC$ as a function of $x$.

b) What is the maximum value of $R$?

Let triangle $ABC$ be isosceles with $AB = AC = 1$ and base $BC = 2x$, where $x > 0$.

a) Determine the area $A$ of $\triangle ABC$ as a function of $x$.

b) What is the maximum value of $A$?

Let triangle $ABC$ be isosceles with $AB = AC = 1$ and base $BC = 2x$, where $x > 0$.

a) Find the inradius $r$ of $\triangle ABC$ as a function of $x$.

b) Determine the minimum possible value of $r$.

positive_text: Let $\triangle ABC$ with $AB \ne AC$ have a circle passing through $A$ that intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at points $M$ and $N$, respectively, and intersects segment $BC$ at points $Q$ and $P$ such that $Q$ is between $B$ and $P$. Suppose $MP \parallel AC$, $NQ \parallel AB$, and the ratio $\frac{BP}{CQ} = \frac{AB}{AC}$. Determine the measure of $\angle BAC$.

negatives.text: A circle through $A$ in triangle $ABC$ intersects $AB$ at $M$, $AC$ at $N$, and $BC$ at $P$ and $Q$, with $Q$ between $B$ and $P$. Suppose $MP \parallel AC$, $NQ \parallel AB$, and $\frac{BP}{CQ} = \frac{AB^2}{AC^2}$. Find $\angle BAC$.

A circle through vertex $A$ of triangle $ABC$ intersects $AB$ at $M$, $AC$ at $N$, and $BC$ at $P$ and $Q$, with $Q$ between $B$ and $P$. Suppose $MP \parallel AC$, $NQ \parallel AB$, and $\frac{BP}{CQ} = \frac{AC}{AB}$. Find $\angle BAC$.

positive_text: Determine all real values of $m$ and $n$ for which the curve $y = x^{3} + m x + n$ intersects the coordinate axes at exactly three points, and these points form the vertices of a right triangle.

negatives.text: Find all values of the real parameters $a$ and $b$ such that the graph of the function $y = x^{3} + a x + b$ has exactly three common points with the coordinate axes and they are vertices of an isosceles triangle.

Find all values of the real parameters $a$ and $b$ such that the graph of the function $y = x^{3} + a x + b$ has exactly three common points with the coordinate axes and they are vertices of a triangle with area 2.

Find all values of the real parameters $a$ and $b$ such that the graph of the function $y = x^{3} + a x + b$ has exactly three common points with the coordinate axes and they are vertices of a triangle with one vertex at the origin.

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. The feet of the perpendiculars from $D$ to $BC$ and $BA$ are labeled $A_1$ and $C_1$, respectively. The line segment $A_1C_1$ intersects diagonal $AC$ at an interior point $B_1$ with $DB_1 \geq DA_1$. Show that $ABCD$ is cyclic if and only if $$\frac{BC}{DA_1} + \frac{BA}{DC_1} = \frac{AC}{DB_1}$$

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. The feet of the perpendiculars from $D$ to $BC$ and $BA$ are labeled $A_1$ and $C_1$, respectively. The line segment $A_1C_1$ intersects diagonal $AC$ at an interior point $B_1$ with $DB_1 > DA_1$. Show that $ABCD$ is cyclic if and only if $$\frac{BC}{DA_1^2} + \frac{BA}{DC_1^2} = \frac{AC}{DB_1^2}$$

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. The feet of the perpendiculars from $D$ to $BC$ and $BA$ are labeled $A_1$ and $C_1$, respectively. The line segment $A_1C_1$ intersects diagonal $AC$ at an interior point $B_1$ with $DB_1 \geq DA_1$. Show that $ABCD$ is cyclic if and only if $$\frac{BC}{DA_1} + \frac{BA}{DC_1} = \frac{AB}{DB_1}$$

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. The feet of the perpendiculars from $D$ to $BC$ and $BA$ are labeled $A_1$ and $C_1$, respectively. The line segment $A_1C_1$ intersects diagonal $AC$ at an interior point $B_1$ with $DB_1 \geq DA_1$. Show that $ABCD$ is cyclic if and only if $$\frac{BD}{DA_1} + \frac{CD}{DC_1} = \frac{AC}{DB_1}$$

positive_text:
How many integer sequences $\{b_{k}\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$ satisfy the recurrence
$$
 b_{k} + b_{k+1} = 2 b_{k+2} b_{k+3} + 2005
$$
for all positive integers $k$?

negatives.text:
Find the number of integer sequences $\{a_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ satisfying
$$
 a_{n} + a_{n+1} = 2 a_{n+2} a_{n+3} - 2005
$$
for all $n$.

How many integer sequences $\{a_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ satisfy
$$
 a_{n} + a_{n+1} = a_{n+2} a_{n+3} + 2005
$$
for all $n$?

Determine the number of integer sequences $\{a_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ such that
$$
 a_{n} + a_{n+1} = 2 a_{n+2} + a_{n+3} + 2005
$$
for all $n$.

positive_text:
Determine all real numbers $ a $ such that the range of the function
$$
f(\theta)=\frac{\sin^{2} \theta - a}{\sin^{3} \theta - (a^{2} + 2)\sin \theta + 2}
$$
includes the interval $ \left[\frac{1}{2}, 2\right] $.

negatives.text:
Find all values of the real parameter $ a $ such that the image of the function
$$
f(x)=\frac{\sin^{2} x + a}{\sin^{3} x - (a^{2} + 2)\sin x + 2}
$$
contains the interval $ \left[\frac{1}{2}, 2\right] $.

Find all values of the real parameter $ a $ such that the image of the function
$$
f(x)=\frac{\sin^{4} x - a}{\sin^{3} x - (a^{2} + 2)\sin x + 2}
$$
contains the interval $ \left[\frac{1}{2}, 2\right] $.

positive_text:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, $B = \{-k, -k+1, \ldots, k-1, k\}$, and $g: B \rightarrow B$ be a function such that $g(g(x)) = -x$ for every $x \in B$.

a) Prove that $k$ must be even.

b) Determine how many such functions $g: B \rightarrow B$ exist with the given property.

negatives.text:
Let $m$ be a positive integer, $A = \{-m, -m+1, \ldots, m-1, m\}$, and $f: A \rightarrow A$ be a function such that $f(f(n)) = n$ for every $n \in A$.

a) Prove that the number $m$ is even.

b) Find the number of all functions $f: A \rightarrow A$ with the required property.

Let $m$ be a positive integer, $A = \{-m, -m+1, \ldots, m-1, m\}$, and $f: A \rightarrow A$ be a function such that $f(f(n)) = -n$ for every $n \in A$ except $n = 0$.

a) Prove that the number $m$ is even.

b) Find the number of all functions $f: A \rightarrow A$ with the required property.

Let $m$ be a positive integer, $A = \{-m, -m+1, \ldots, m-1, m\}$, and $f: A \rightarrow A$ be a function such that $f(f(n)) = -n$ for every $n \in A$.

a) Prove that the number $m$ is odd.

b) Find the number of all functions $f: A \rightarrow A$ with the required property.

positive_text: Is there a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers $\{b_{k}\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$ such that $b_{k} \leq k^{3}$ for all $k$ and every positive integer can be represented in exactly one way as $b_{i} - b_{j}$ for some $i > j$?

negatives.text: Does there exist a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers $\{d_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ such that $d_{n} \leq n^{3}$ for every $n$ and every positive integer can be written in at least one way as a difference of two terms of the sequence?

Is there a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers $\{e_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ such that $e_{n} \leq n^{3}$ for every $n$ and every positive integer can be written in a unique way as the sum of two terms of the sequence?

positive_text: Suppose $\triangle ABC$ is rotated about point $C$ to form $\triangle A'B'C$. Let $M$, $E$, and $F$ be the midpoints of $BA'$, $AC$, and $B'C$, respectively. Given that $AC \neq BC$ and the distances from $E$ and $F$ to $M$ are equal, determine the measure of $\angle EMF$.

negatives.text: Suppose $\triangle ABC$ is reflected over point $C$ to form $\triangle A'B'C$. Let $M$, $E$, and $F$ be the midpoints of $BA'$, $AC$, and $B'C$, respectively. Given that $AC \neq BC$ and $EM = FM$, determine $\angle EMF$.

Let $\triangle A'B'C$ be the image of $\triangle ABC$ under a rotation with center $C$. Let $M$, $E$, and $F$ be the midpoints of $AB'$, $AC$, and $B'C$, respectively. If $AC \neq BC$ and $EM = FM$, find $\angle EMF$.

Let $\triangle A'B'C$ be the image of $\triangle ABC$ under a rotation with center $C$. Let $M$, $E$, and $F$ be the midpoints of $BA'$, $AC$, and $B'C$, respectively. If $AC = BC$ and $EM = FM$, find $\angle EMF$.

positive_text: Let $ x $, $ m $, and $ n $ be positive integers. Consider a game where two players alternate subtracting either $ m $ or $ n $ from $ x $. The player who causes the result to go below zero loses. Prove that there are infinitely many values of $ x $ such that the first player has a winning strategy for any such game with $ m + n = 2005 $.

negatives.text: Let $ t $, $ a $, and $ b $ be positive integers. Consider a game where two players alternate adding $ a $ or $ b $ to $ t $, instead of subtracting. The player who causes the number to exceed 2005 wins. Prove that there are infinitely many $ t $ such that the first player has a winning strategy.

Let $ t $, $ a $, and $ b $ be positive integers. Two players alternate subtracting $ a $ or $ b $ from $ t $, but they can only subtract $ a $ on odd-numbered turns and $ b $ on even-numbered turns. The player who causes the number to go below zero loses. Prove that there are infinitely many $ t $ such that the first player has a winning strategy.

Let $ t $, $ a $, and $ b $ be positive integers. Two players alternate subtracting $ a $ or $ b $ from $ t $, but now the player who reaches zero exactly wins the game. Prove that there are infinitely many $ t $ such that the first player has a winning strategy.

positive_text: Suppose there are $n$ knights and $m$ maidens, with $m \geq 2n - 1$. Each knight is acquainted with some subset of the maidens. Show that it is possible to pair each knight with a maiden so that either the knight knows his maiden, or all the maidens he knows are not paired with any knight.

negatives.text: In a group of $B$ boys and $G$ girls, where $G < 2B - 1$, some boys know some girls. Is it still possible to pair all boys with girls so that each boy who does not know his pair only knows girls who are not dancing?

positive_text:

a) Prove that the equation $g(x) = 0$ has two distinct real roots $r_{1}$ and $r_{2}$.

b) Find all values of $b$ such that $r_{1}^{3} + r_{2}^{3} = -72$.

negatives.text:

a) Prove that the equation $f(x) = 0$ has two distinct real roots $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$.

b) Find all values of $a$ such that $x_{1}^{3} + x_{2}^{3} = -72$.

b) Find all values of $a$ such that $x_{1}^{3} + x_{2}^{3} = -72a$.

positive_text: Determine all real values of the parameter $a$ such that the quadratics $x^{2} - (2a+1)x + a = 0$ and $x^{2} + (a-4)x + (a-1) = 0$ have real roots $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma, \delta$, respectively, and satisfy the identity $$\frac{\alpha}{\gamma} + \frac{\delta}{\beta} = \frac{\alpha \delta (\alpha + \beta + \gamma + \delta)}{a}$$

negatives.text: Find all real values of $a$ such that the equations $x^{2}-(2a+1)x+a=0$ and $x^{2}+(a-4)x+a-1=0$ have real roots $x_{1}, x_{2}$ and $x_{3}, x_{4}$, respectively, and satisfy the identity $$\frac{x_{1}}{x_{3}} + \frac{x_{4}}{x_{2}} = \frac{x_{1} x_{4}(x_{1}x_{2} + x_{3}x_{4})}{a}$$

Find all real values of $a$ such that the equations $x^{2}-(2a+1)x+a=0$ and $x^{2}+(a-4)x+a-1=0$ have real roots $x_{1}, x_{2}$ and $x_{3}, x_{4}$, respectively, and satisfy the identity $$\frac{x_{1}}{x_{3}} + \frac{x_{4}}{x_{2}} = \frac{x_{1} x_{4}(x_{1}+x_{2}+x_{3}+x_{4})}{a^{2}}$$

Find all real values of $a$ such that the equations $x^{2}-(2a+1)x+a=0$ and $x^{2}+(a-4)x+a-1=0$ have real roots $x_{1}, x_{2}$ and $x_{3}, x_{4}$, respectively, and satisfy the identity $$\frac{x_{1}}{x_{3}} + \frac{x_{4}}{x_{2}} = \frac{x_{1} x_{4}(x_{1}+x_{2}+x_{3}+x_{4})}{a} + 1$$

positive_text: In triangle $PQR$, the centroid is $M$ and the incenter is $N$. It is given that $PQ = 42$, $MN = 2$, and $PQ \parallel MN$. Determine the lengths of $PR$ and $QR$.

negatives.text: In triangle $ABC$, centroid $G$ and incenter $I$ are given. If $AB = 42$, $GI = 2$ and $AB \perp GI$, find $AC$ and $BC$.

positive_text: Determine all four-digit numbers $ a $ less than $ 2005 $ for which there exists a positive integer $ b < a $ such that $ ab $ is a perfect square and $ a - b $ has no more than three unique positive divisors.

negatives.text: Find all four-digit positive integers $ m $ less than $ 2005 $ for which there exists a positive integer $ n < m $, such that $ m + n $ is a perfect square and $ m - n $ has at most three distinct positive divisors.

Determine all four-digit positive integers $ m $ less than $ 2005 $ for which there exists a positive integer $ n < m $, such that $ mn $ is a perfect square and $ m - n $ has exactly three distinct positive divisors.

Find all four-digit positive integers $ m $ less than $ 2005 $ for which there exists a positive integer $ n < m $, such that $ mn $ is a perfect square and $ m + n $ has at most three distinct positive divisors.

positive_text: Determine all real values of $ a $ for which the equation $ |x^{2} - a x - 2a + 1| = a - 1 $ has four real solutions $ x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, x_{4} $ satisfying $$ x_{1}^{2} + x_{2}^{2} + x_{3}^{2} + x_{4}^{2} = 20 $$

negatives.text: Find all values of the real parameter $ p $ such that the equation $ |x^{2} - p x - 2p + 1| = p $ has four real roots $ x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, x_{4} $ such that $$ x_{1}^{2} + x_{2}^{2} + x_{3}^{2} + x_{4}^{2} = 20 $$

Find all values of the real parameter $ p $ such that the equation $ |x^{2} - p x - 2p + 1| = p - 1 $ has four real roots $ x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, x_{4} $ such that $$ x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3} + x_{4} = 20 $$

Find all values of the real parameter $ p $ such that the equation $ |x^{2} - p x - 2p| = p - 1 $ has four real roots $ x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, x_{4} $ such that $$ x_{1}^{2} + x_{2}^{2} + x_{3}^{2} + x_{4}^{2} = 20 $$

positive_text: \text{Given the inequality } \sqrt{t} + \sqrt{2 - t} \geq \sqrt{b}, \text{ where } b \text{ is a real number.} \quad \text{a) Solve the inequality for } b = 3. \quad \text{б) Determine all } b, \text{ for which the solution set of the inequality is an interval of length at most } \sqrt{3}.

negatives.text: \text{Consider the inequality } \sqrt{x} + \sqrt{2 - x} \geq \sqrt{a}, \text{ where } a \text{ is a real number.} \quad \text{a) Solve for } a = 3. \quad \text{б) Find all } a, \text{ for which the solution set is an interval of length } < \sqrt{3}.

positive_text:
Let $g(x)$ be defined as
$$
g(x) = \frac{x^{2} - 2006x + 1}{x^{2} + 1}
$$

a. Determine the values of $x$ for which $g'(x) \geq 0$.

b. Show that $|g(x) - g(y)| \leq 2006$ for all real $x$ and $y$.

negatives.text:

b. Prove that $|q(x) - q(y)| \leq 2006$ for all real $x$ and $y$.

$$
r(x) = \frac{x^{2} - 2006x + 1}{x^{2} + 1}
$$
