positive_text: Let $b$ be a real number with $b \ge 1$. Define a sequence $(y_n)_{n \ge 1}$ by $y_1 = b$ and $y_{n+1} = 1 + \log_2 y_n$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}^*$. Find all values of $b$ for which every term in the sequence is a rational number.

negatives.text: Let $a \ge 1$ be a real number. The sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 1}$ is defined by $x_1 = a$ and $x_{n+1} = 1 + \log_2(x_n + 1)$. Find all values of $a$ such that all terms of the sequence are rational.
Let $a \ge 1$ be a real number. The sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 1}$ is defined by $x_1 = a$ and $x_{n+1} = 1 + \log_3 x_n$. Determine all values of $a$ for which every term in the sequence is rational.
Let $a \ge 1$ be a real number. The sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 1}$ is defined by $x_1 = a$ and $x_{n+1} = 1 + \log_2 x_n$. Find all values of $a$ such that all terms of the sequence are integers.

positive_text: Fie triunghiul ascuțitunghic $PQR$ cu centrul cercului circumscris notat $O$ și $S$ proiecția punctului $P$ pe latura $QR$. Știind că $OS \parallel PR$, demonstrați că $\sin 2Q = \operatorname{ctg} R$.

negatives.text: Fie triunghiul ascuțitunghic $ABC$ cu centrul cercului circumscris $O$ și $D$ piciorul înălțimii din $A$. Știind că $OD \parallel AC$, arătați că $\sin 2B = \operatorname{ctg} C$.
Fie triunghiul ascuțitunghic $ABC$ cu centrul cercului circumscris $O$ și $D$ piciorul înălțimii din $A$. Știind că $OD \parallel AB$, arătați că $\sin B = \operatorname{ctg} C$.

positive_text: Fie $x, y, z > 0$ cu $x + y + z = 1$. Demonstrați că: $$\frac{1}{x + yz} + \frac{1}{y + zx} + \frac{1}{z + xy} \geqslant \frac{7}{1 + xyz}$$

negatives.text: Fie $a, b, c > 0$ cu $a + b + c = 1$. Demonstrați că: $$\frac{1}{a + b + c} + \frac{1}{b + c + a} + \frac{1}{c + a + b} \geqslant \frac{7}{1 + abc}$$
Fie $a, b, c > 0$ cu $a + b + c = 1$. Demonstrați că: $$\frac{1}{a + bc} + \frac{1}{b + ca} + \frac{1}{c + ab} \geqslant \frac{7}{1 - abc}$$
Fie $a, b, c > 0$ cu $a + b + c = 2$. Demonstrați că: $$\frac{1}{a + bc} + \frac{1}{b + ca} + \frac{1}{c + ab} \geqslant \frac{7}{1 + abc}$$

positive_text: \text{Determinați perechile } (a, b) \text{ de numere naturale nenule cu } a \leq b, \text{ astfel încât} \quad \frac{(a+b)(a b - 1)}{a b + 1} \text{ este un număr prim}.

negatives.text: \text{Aflați numerele naturale nenule } x, y \text{ cu } x \leq y, \text{ astfel încât} \quad \frac{(x+y)(x y + 1)}{x y - 1} = p, \quad \text{unde } p \text{ este un număr prim}.
\text{Aflați numerele naturale nenule } x, y \text{ cu } x \leq y, \text{ astfel încât} \quad \frac{(x+y)(x y - 1)}{x y + 1} = p^2, \quad \text{unde } p \text{ este un număr prim}.
\text{Aflați numerele naturale nenule } x, y \text{ cu } x \leq y, \text{ astfel încât} \quad \frac{(x+y)(x y - 1)}{x y + 1} = p, \quad \text{unde } p \text{ este un număr impar}.

positive_text: Fie $p, q, r, s \in \mathbb{N}$, $s \neq 0$ şi fie funcţia $g: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$, definită prin $$ g(n) = \left[ \frac{p n + q}{r n + s} \right], \text{ oricare ar fi } n \in \mathbb{N} $$ unde $[x]$ este partea întreagă a numărului real $x$. Demonstraţi că următoarele afirmaţii sunt echivalente: $1^\circ$ $g$ este surjectivă. $2^\circ$ $r = 0$, $q < s$ şi $0 < p \leq s$.

negatives.text: Fie $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{N}$, $d \neq 0$ şi fie funcţia $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$, definită prin $$ f(n) = \left[ \frac{a n + b}{c n + d} \right], \text{ oricare ar fi } n \in \mathbb{N} $$ unde $[x]$ este partea întreagă a numărului real $x$. Demonstraţi că următoarele afirmaţii sunt echivalente: $1^\circ$ $f$ este surjectivă. $2^\circ$ $c = 1$, $b < d$ şi $0 < a \leq d$.

Fie $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{N}$, $d \neq 0$ şi fie funcţia $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$, definită prin $$ f(n) = \left[ \frac{a n + b}{c n + d} \right], \text{ oricare ar fi } n \in \mathbb{N} $$ unde $[x]$ este partea întreagă a numărului real $x$. Demonstraţi că următoarele afirmaţii sunt echivalente: $1^\circ$ $f$ este injectivă. $2^\circ$ $c = 0$, $b < d$ şi $0 < a \leq d$.

positive_text: Fie $n \geq 2$ și $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$ numere reale nenule, nu neapărat distincte. Se definește matricea $B=\left(b_{ij}\right)_{1 \leq i, j \leq n} \in M_{n}(\mathbb{R})$ prin $b_{ij}=\max \{b_{i}, b_{j}\}$, pentru orice $i, j \in\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$. Demonstrați că $\operatorname{rang}(B)=\operatorname{card}\left\{b_{k} \mid k=1,2, \ldots, n\right\}$.

negatives.text: Fie $n \geq 2$ și $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ numere reale nenule, nu neapărat distincte. Se definește matricea $A=\left(a_{ij}\right)_{1 \leq i, j \leq n} \in M_{n}(\mathbb{R})$ prin $a_{ij}=\min \{a_{i}, a_{j}\}$, pentru orice $i, j \in\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$. Demonstrați că $\operatorname{rang}(A)=\operatorname{card}\left\{a_{k} \mid k=1,2, \ldots, n\right\}$.

Fie $n \geq 2$ și $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ numere reale nenule, nu neapărat distincte. Se definește matricea $A=\left(a_{ij}\right)_{1 \leq i, j \leq n} \in M_{n}(\mathbb{R})$ prin $a_{ij}=\max \{a_{i}, a_{j}\}$, pentru orice $i, j \in\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$. Demonstrați că $\operatorname{rang}(A) \leq \operatorname{card}\left\{a_{k} \mid k=1,2, \ldots, n\right\}$.

Fie $n \geq 2$ și $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ numere reale nenule, nu neapărat distincte. Se definește matricea $A=\left(a_{ij}\right)_{1 \leq i, j \leq n} \in M_{n}(\mathbb{R})$ prin $a_{ij}=\max \{a_{i}, a_{j}\}$, pentru orice $i, j \in\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$. Demonstrați că $\operatorname{rang}(A) \geq \operatorname{card}\left\{a_{k} \mid k=1,2, \ldots, n\right\}$.

positive_text: Fie $x, y, z$ numere strict pozitive cu $x + y + z = 1$. Demonstrați că $$\frac{1}{x y z}+\frac{4}{x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}} \geq \frac{13}{x y+y z+z x}$$

negatives.text: Fie $a, b, c$ numere strict pozitive astfel încât $a+b+c=1$. Demonstrați că $$\frac{1}{a b c}+\frac{4}{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}} \leq \frac{13}{a b+b c+c a}$$
Fie $a, b, c$ numere strict pozitive astfel încât $a+b+c=1$. Demonstrați că $$\frac{1}{a b c}+\frac{4}{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}} \geq \frac{13}{a+b+c a}$$
Fie $a, b, c$ numere strict pozitive astfel încât $a+b+c=1$. Demonstrați că $$\frac{1}{a b c}+\frac{4}{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}} \geq \frac{13}{a b+b c}$$

positive_text: Fie $n \geq 2$ un număr natural cu proprietatea că mulţimea $\{ z \in \mathbb{C} \mid z^n = 1 \}$ are mai puţin de $2^{[\sqrt{n}]} - 1$ submulţimi cu suma elementelor egală cu zero. Demonstrați că $n$ este număr prim.

negatives.text: Fie $n \geq 2$ un număr natural cu proprietatea că mulţimea rădăcinilor de ordin $n$ ale unităţii are mai puţin de $2^{[\sqrt{n}]} - 1$ submulţimi cu produsul elementelor egal cu 1. Arătați că $n$ este prim.

positive_text:
Fie $g: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ o funcție derivabilă de ordinul $m \geq 2$, astfel încât
$$
\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} g(x)=L \in \mathbb{R} \text{ și } \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} g^{(m)}(x)=0
$$
Demonstrați că $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} g^{(j)}(x)=0$, pentru orice $j \in\{1,2, \ldots, m-1\}$, unde $g^{(j)}$ este derivata de ordinul $j$ a funcției $g$.

negatives.text:
Fie $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ o funcție derivabilă de ordinul $n \geq 2$, astfel încât
$$
\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} f(x)=\ell \in \mathbb{R} \text{ și } \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} f^{(n)}(x)=1
$$
Demonstrați că $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} f^{(k)}(x)=0$, pentru orice $k \in\{1,2, \ldots, n-1\}$, unde $f^{(k)}$ reprezintă derivata de ordinul $k$ a funcției $f$.

Fie $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ o funcție derivabilă de ordinul $n \geq 2$, astfel încât
$$
\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} f(x)=\ell \in \mathbb{R} \text{ și } \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} f^{(n)}(x) = \infty
$$
Demonstrați că $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} f^{(k)}(x)=0$, pentru orice $k \in\{1,2, \ldots, n-1\}$, unde $f^{(k)}$ reprezintă derivata de ordinul $k$ a funcției $f$.

positive_text:
Fie $a \in \mathbb{N}$, $a > 2$. Să se demonstreze că

a) Există un număr natural $m > 1$, compus, astfel încât $a^m \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$.

b) Dacă $q$ este cel mai mic număr natural $q > 1$ cu proprietatea $a^q \equiv 1 \pmod{q}$, atunci $q$ este prim.

c) Nu există numere $m > 1$ astfel încât $2^m \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$.

negatives.text:
Fie $a \in \mathbb{N}$, $a > 2$. Să se demonstreze că

a) Există un număr natural $n > 1$, compus, astfel încât $a^n \equiv -1 \pmod{n}$.

b) Dacă $p$ este cel mai mic număr natural $p > 1$ cu proprietatea $a^p \equiv -1 \pmod{p}$, atunci $p$ este prim.

c) Nu există numere $n > 1$ astfel încât $2^n \equiv -1 \pmod{n}$.

Fie $a \in \mathbb{N}$, $a > 2$. Să se demonstreze că

a) Există un număr natural $n > 1$, compus, astfel încât $a^n \equiv 1 \pmod{n^2}$.

b) Dacă $p$ este cel mai mic număr natural $p > 1$ cu proprietatea $a^p \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$, atunci $p$ este prim.

c) Nu există numere $n > 1$ astfel încât $2^n \equiv 1 \pmod{n^2}$.

Fie $a \in \mathbb{N}$, $a > 2$. Să se demonstreze că

a) Există un număr natural $n > 1$, compus, astfel încât $a^n \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$ și $n$ este putere de prim.

b) Dacă $p$ este cel mai mic număr natural $p > 1$ cu proprietatea $a^p \equiv 1 \pmod{p}$, atunci $p$ este putere de prim.

c) Nu există numere $n > 1$ astfel încât $2^n \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$ și $n$ este putere de prim.

positive_text: Fie $n \geq 2$ şi $C, D \in M_{n}(\mathbb{R})$. Să presupunem că există un număr real $y \in \mathbb{R} \setminus\left\{0, \frac{1}{2}, 1\right\}$ cu proprietatea că $y C D + (1 - y) D C = I_{n}$. Demonstrați că $(C D - D C)^{n} = O_{n}$.

negatives.text: Fie $n \geq 2$ şi $S, T \in M_{n}(\mathbb{R})$. Presupunem că există $u \in \mathbb{R} \setminus\left\{0, \frac{1}{2}, 1\right\}$ astfel încât $u S T + (1 - u) T S = I_{n}$. Arătați că $(S T + T S)^{n} = O_{n}$.

positive_text: Fie $S$ o mulțime finită de numere naturale. Găsiți toate funcțiile $g: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow S$ astfel încât $g(|a-b|) = |g(a) - g(b)|$ pentru orice $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$.

negatives.text: Fie $A$ o mulțime finită de numere naturale. Găsiți toate funcțiile $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow A$ astfel încât $f(|x-y|) = f(x) - f(y)$ pentru orice $x, y \in \mathbb{N}$.
Fie $A$ o mulțime finită de numere naturale. Găsiți toate funcțiile $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow A$ astfel încât $f(x+y) = |f(x) - f(y)|$ pentru orice $x, y \in \mathbb{N}$.

positive_text: Pe o tablă pătrată de dimensiune $n \times n$, cu $n \geq 2$, se plasează $n$ piese identice, aşa încât nicio două să nu fie în aceeaşi linie sau coloană. Fiecare piesă se poate deplasa simultan într-o poziție adiacentă (cu o latură comună). Determinați toate valorile $n$ pentru care există o configurație inițială care permite o astfel de mutare simultană, astfel încât piesele să nu se atace după deplasare.

negatives.text: Pe o tablă $n \times n$, cu $n \geq 2$, se amplasează $n$ obiecte astfel încât nicio două să nu fie în aceeași linie sau coloană. Toate obiectele se mișcă simultan o dată, fiecare doar într-o poziție adiacentă (cu o latură comună). Determinați toate valorile $n$ pentru care există o amplasare inițială care permite o astfel de mișcare, astfel încât, după aceasta, toate obiectele să se afle în aceeași linie sau coloană.

Pe o tablă $n \times n$, cu $n \geq 2$, se amplasează $n$ obiecte astfel încât nicio două să nu fie în aceeași linie sau coloană. Toate obiectele se mișcă simultan o dată, fiecare doar într-o poziție adiacentă (cu o latură comună). Determinați toate valorile $n$ pentru care există o amplasare inițială care permite o astfel de mișcare, astfel încât, după aceasta, toate obiectele să fie pe poziții de culori alternante (negre și albe).

Pe o tablă $n \times n$, cu $n \geq 2$, se amplasează $n$ obiecte astfel încât nicio două să nu fie în aceeași linie sau coloană. Toate obiectele se mișcă simultan o dată, fiecare doar într-o poziție adiacentă (cu o latură comună). Determinați toate valorile $n$ pentru care există o amplasare inițială care permite o astfel de mișcare, astfel încât, după aceasta, toate obiectele să se afle pe poziții diagonale.

positive_text: Fie $N \geq 4$ un număr natural fixat. Doi jucători, $X$ şi $Y$, construiesc un șir $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots$, unde $X$ alege $a_{1} = 1$ sau $-1$, apoi $Y$ alege $a_{2} = 2$ sau $-2$, și așa mai departe; la pasul $k$, $a_k$ este $k$ sau $-k$. Câştigătorul este cel care creează prima o subsecvență consecutivă al cărei sumă este divizibilă cu $N$ (inclusiv un singur element). Pentru fiecare $N$, determinați care jucător are strategie câştigătoare.

negatives.text: Doi jucători, $P$ și $Q$, construiesc un șir $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots$, unde pe rând fiecare alege $a_k$ să fie $k^2$ sau $-k^2$. Câştigătorul este cel care creează prima o subsecvență consecutivă al cărei sumă este divizibilă cu $N$, un număr fixat $\geq 4$. Pentru fiecare $N$, determinați cine are o strategie câştigătoare.

Doi jucători, $R$ și $S$, construiesc un șir $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots$, unde pe rând fiecare alege $a_k$ să fie $k$ sau $-k$. Câştigătorul este cel care creează prima o subsecvență consecutivă al cărei produs este divizibil cu $N$, un număr fixat $\geq 4$. Pentru fiecare $N$, determinați cine are o strategie câştigătoare.

Doi jucători, $U$ și $V$, construiesc un șir $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots$, unde pe rând fiecare alege $a_k$ să fie $k$ sau $-k$. Câştigătorul este cel care creează prima o subsecvență consecutivă al cărei sumă este egală cu $N$, un număr fixat $\geq 4$. Pentru fiecare $N$, determinați cine are o strategie câştigătoare.

positive_text: Fie $ABC$ un triunghi dreptunghic în $A$, cu $BC$ ca ipotenuză. Fie $A'$ mijlocul lui $BC$, $D$ piciorul înălțimii din $A$, iar $M$ mijlocul segmentului $AD$. Dacă $P$ este punctul de intersecție al dreptelor $BM$ și $AA'$, și $\alpha = m(\widehat{PCB})$, demonstrați că $$ \operatorname{tg} \alpha = \sin C \cdot \cos C $$

negatives.text: Fie $ABC$ un triunghi isoscel cu $AB = AC$. Fie $A'$ mijlocul lui $BC$, $D$ piciorul înălțimii din $A$, iar $M$ mijlocul segmentului $AD$. Dacă $P = BM \cap AA'$, și $\alpha = m(\widehat{PCB})$, demonstrați că $$ \operatorname{tg} \alpha = \sin C \cdot \cos C $$

positive_text:
Fie $n \geq 2$ un număr întreg și o matrice $A = (a_{ij})$ cu $n \times n$ elemente reale strict pozitive, astfel încât:
(1) $a_{ii} = 1$ pentru toți $i$;
(2) pentru fiecare $j = 2, \ldots, n$, șirul $a_{1j}, a_{2j}, \ldots, a_{j-1,j}$ este o permutare a șirului $\frac{1}{a_{j1}}, \frac{1}{a_{j2}}, \ldots, \frac{1}{a_{j,j-1}}$.
Dacă $s_i = \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij}$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$, determinați valoarea maximă a $\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{s_i}$.

negatives.text:
Fie $n \geq 2$ un număr întreg și o matrice $A = (a_{ij})$ cu $n \times n$ elemente reale strict pozitive, astfel încât:
(1) $a_{ii} = 2$ pentru toți $i$;
(2) pentru fiecare $j = 2, \ldots, n$, șirul $a_{1j}, a_{2j}, \ldots, a_{j-1,j}$ este o permutare a șirului $\frac{1}{a_{j1}}, \frac{1}{a_{j2}}, \ldots, \frac{1}{a_{j,j-1}}$.
Fie $s_i = \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij}$. Determinați valoarea maximă a $\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{s_i}$.

Fie $n \geq 2$ un număr întreg și o matrice $A = (a_{ij})$ cu $n \times n$ elemente reale strict pozitive, astfel încât:
(1) $a_{ii} = 1$ pentru toți $i$;
(2) pentru fiecare $j = 2, \ldots, n$, șirul $a_{1j}, a_{2j}, \ldots, a_{j-1,j}$ este o permutare a șirului $\frac{1}{a_{j1}}, \frac{1}{a_{j2}}, \ldots, \frac{1}{a_{j,j-1}}$.
Fie $s_i = \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij}$. Determinați valoarea maximă a $\sum_{i=1}^{n} s_i$.

positive_text: Aflați toate funcțiile $ h: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ astfel încât există $ k: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ cu proprietatea că $$ h(a) + h(b) = [k(a + b)] $$ pentru orice $ a, b \in \mathbb{R} $. (Notăm cu $ [x] $ partea întreagă a numărului real $ x $.)

negatives.text: Determinați funcțiile $ f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ pentru care există funcția $ g: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ astfel încât $$ f(x) + f(y) = g([x + y]) $$ pentru orice $ x, y \in \mathbb{R} $.

Determinați funcțiile $ f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ pentru care există funcția $ g: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ astfel încât $$ f(x) + f(y) = g(x) + g(y) $$ pentru orice $ x, y \in \mathbb{R} $.

Determinați funcțiile $ f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ pentru care există funcția $ g: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ astfel încât $$ f(x) + f(y) = [g(x) + g(y)] $$ pentru orice $ x, y \in \mathbb{R} $.

positive_text:
Fie $p, q, r, s$ numere întregi pozitive, cu $p < q < r < s$ și $p s = q r$. Demonstrați că
$$
2 p + \sqrt{p} + \sqrt{s} < q + r + 1
$$

negatives.text:
Fie $a, b, c, d$ numere întregi pozitive, cu $a < b < c < d$ și $a d = b c$. Demonstrați că
$$
2 a + \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{d} < b + c
$$

Fie $a, b, c, d$ numere întregi pozitive, cu $a < b < c < d$ și $a^2 d = b c$. Demonstrați că
$$
2 a + \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{d} < b + c + 1
$$

Fie $a, b, c, d$ numere întregi pozitive, cu $a < b < c < d$ și $a d = b c$. Demonstrați că
$$
2 a + a + d < b + c + 1
$$

positive_text: Dacă $N$ este un număr întreg care poate fi scris ca suma a trei pătrate, atunci $N$ poate fi exprimat sub forma $$ N = \frac{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} + w^{2}}{1 + xyzw} $$ unde $x, y, z, w$ sunt numere întregi pozitive. Este adevărată reciproca acestei afirmații?

negatives.text: Orice număr întreg $N$, care este suma a trei pătrate perfecte, este evident exprimabil sub forma $$ N = \frac{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} + d^{2}}{1 + abcd} $$ unde $a, b, c, d$ sunt numere întregi. Este adevărată afirmația reciprocă?

Orice număr întreg $N$, care este suma a trei pătrate perfecte, este evident exprimabil sub forma $$ N = \frac{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} + d^{2}}{1 + abcd} $$ unde $a, b, c, d$ sunt numere naturale. Este adevărată afirmația reciprocă pentru numere strict pozitive?

Orice număr întreg $N$, care este suma a două pătrate perfecte, este evident exprimabil sub forma $$ N = \frac{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} + d^{2}}{1 + abcd} $$ unde $a, b, c, d$ sunt numere naturale. Este adevărată afirmația reciprocă?

positive_text: Fie $a, b$ numere întregi cu $a, b \geq 2$. Într-un grid rectangular cu coloane $1$ la $a$ și linii $1$ la $b$, considerăm un subset $T$ de puncte laticiale. Dacă $|T| \geq a+b+\left\lfloor \frac{1}{4} a+\frac{1}{4} b-\frac{1}{2} \right\rfloor$, arătați că există un cerc care conține cel puțin patru puncte din $T$, distincte două câte două.

negatives.text: Fie $S$ o mulțime de puncte laticiale în $[1, m] \times [1, n]$, cu $m, n \geq 2$. Dacă $|S| \geq m+n+\left\lfloor \frac{1}{2} m+\frac{1}{2} n-\frac{1}{2} \right\rfloor$, arătați că există un cerc care trece prin cel puțin patru puncte din $S$.

Fie $S$ o mulțime de puncte laticiale în $[1, m] \times [1, n]$, cu $m, n \geq 2$. Dacă $|S| \geq m+n+\left\lfloor \frac{1}{4} m+\frac{1}{4} n-\frac{1}{2} \right\rfloor$, arătați că există o dreaptă care trece prin cel puțin patru puncte din $S$.

positive_text: Let $ a $ and $ b $ be positive integers such that $ a < 2^b $. Find the minimum number of (not necessarily distinct) powers of 2 whose sum equals $ a \cdot (2^b - 1) $.

negatives.text: Let $ m $ and $ n $ be positive integers with $ m < 2^n $. Find the minimum number of distinct powers of 2 that sum to $ m \cdot (2^n + 1) $.
Let $ m $ and $ n $ be positive integers with $ m < 2^n $. Find the minimum number of not necessarily distinct powers of 2 that sum to $ m \cdot (2^n - 1) + 1 $.
Let $ m $ and $ n $ be positive integers with $ m < 2^n $. Find the minimum number of not necessarily distinct powers of 3 that sum to $ m \cdot (2^n - 1) $.

positive_text:
Let $b_k = \{\sqrt{k-2}\} - \{\sqrt{k-1}\} + \{\sqrt{k}\} - \{\sqrt{k+1}\}$, where $\{x\}$ denotes the fractional part of the real number $x$.

a) Prove that $b_3 > 0.2$.

b) Prove that $b_k < 0$, for infinitely many $k$, and $b_k > 0$, for infinitely many $k$.

negatives.text:
Let $c_n = \{\sqrt{n}\} + \{\sqrt{n+1}\} - \{\sqrt{n+2}\} - \{\sqrt{n+3}\}$, where $\{x\}$ denotes the fractional part of the real number $x$.

a) Prove that $c_1 > 0.2$.

b) Prove that $c_n < 0$, for infinitely many $n$, and $c_n > 0$, for infinitely many $n$.

Let $d_n = \{\sqrt{n}\} - \{\sqrt{n+1}\} + \{\sqrt{n+2}\} - \{\sqrt{n+3}\}$, where $\{x\}$ denotes the fractional part of the real number $x$.

a) Prove that $d_1 < 0.2$.

b) Prove that $d_n < 0$, for all $n$.

positive_text: Find all non-negative integers $n$ for which there exist integers $x$ and $y$ satisfying $x + 2^y = n^{2022}$ and $x^2 + 4^y = n^{2023}$.

negatives.text: Find all non-negative integers $n$ for which there exist integers $a$ and $b$ such that $a + 2^b = n^{2022}$ and $a^2 + 4^b = n^{2021}$.
Find all non-negative integers $n$ for which there exist integers $a$ and $b$ such that $a - 2^b = n^{2022}$ and $a^2 + 4^b = n^{2023}$.
Find all non-negative integers $n$ for which there exist integers $a$ and $b$ such that $a + 2^b = n^{2022}$ and $a^2 + 2^b = n^{2023}$.

positive_text: Determine all positive real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ such that $$ abc \le \min \left\{ 4 \left(a - \frac{1}{b}\right), 4 \left(b - \frac{1}{c}\right), 4 \left(c - \frac{1}{a}\right) \right\}. $$

negatives.text: Find all positive real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ such that $$ xyz \le \min \left\{ 4 \left(x + \frac{1}{y}\right), 4 \left(y + \frac{1}{z}\right), 4 \left(z + \frac{1}{x}\right) \right\}. $$
Find all positive real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ such that $$ xyz \le \min \left\{ 4 \left(x - y\right), 4 \left(y - z\right), 4 \left(z - x\right) \right\}. $$
Find all positive real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ such that $$ xyz \le \min \left\{ 4 \left(x - \frac{1}{y^2}\right), 4 \left(y - \frac{1}{z^2}\right), 4 \left(z - \frac{1}{x^2}\right) \right\}. $$

positive_text: Find all continuous functions $ g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} $ satisfying $ g(1) = e $ and $ g(x + y) = e^{3xy} \cdot g(x) \cdot g(y) $ for all real numbers $ x $ and $ y $.

negatives.text: Find all continuous functions $ f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} $ satisfying $ f(1) = e $ and $ f(x + y) = e^{3(x + y)} \cdot f(x) \cdot f(y) $ for all $ x, y \in \mathbb{R} $.
Find all continuous functions $ f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} $ satisfying $ f(1) = e $ and $ f(x + y) = e^{3x^2} \cdot f(x) \cdot f(y) $ for all $ x, y \in \mathbb{R} $.

positive_text:
Let $(H, \star)$ be a finite group of size $n \in \mathbb{N}^*$, where $n \ge 2$. We define $(H, \star)$ to be *cyclically arrangeable* if there exists a sequence of elements $h_1, h_2, \dots, h_n$ such that the set of all products $h_i \star h_{i+1}$ (with $h_{n+1} = h_1$) is equal to the entire group $H$.

a) For which positive integers $n$ is the group $(\mathbb{Z}_n, +)$ cyclically arrangeable?

b) Provide an example of a cyclically arrangeable group of even size.

negatives.text:
Let $(G, \cdot)$ be a finite group of order $n \in \mathbb{N}^*$, with $n \ge 2$. We call $(G, \cdot)$ *multiplicatively arrangeable* if there is an ordering $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ such that the set of all *powers* $a_i^2$ for $1 \le i \le n$ is equal to the entire group $G$.

a) For which positive integers $n$ is the group $(\mathbb{Z}_n, +)$ multiplicatively arrangeable?

b) Give an example of a multiplicatively arrangeable group of even order.

Let $(G, \cdot)$ be a finite group of order $n \in \mathbb{N}^*$, with $n \ge 2$. We say $(G, \cdot)$ is *pairwise arrangeable* if there is a subset $\{a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k\}$ with $k < n$ such that the set of all products $a_i \cdot a_j$ for $1 \le i, j \le k$ is equal to the entire group $G$.

a) For which positive integers $n$ is the group $(\mathbb{Z}_n, +)$ pairwise arrangeable?

b) Give an example of a pairwise arrangeable group of even order.

positive_text: Find all real values of $x$ satisfying the equation $2^{x - 1} + 2^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}} = 3$.

negatives.text: Solve in real numbers the equation $2^{x-1} + 2^{-\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}} = 3$.
Solve in real numbers the equation $2^{x-1} + 2^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}} = 4$.

positive_text:
In triangle $\triangle XYZ$,
a) Demonstrate that the internal angle bisector of $\angle X$ and the external bisectors of $\angle Y$ and $\angle Z$ meet at a point $J_X$.
b) Let $J_X M' \perp XZ$, $M' \in XZ$, $J_X N' \perp YZ$, $N' \in YZ$, and $J_X P' \perp XY$, $P' \in XY$. Prove that if $J_X M' + J_X P' = J_X N'$, then triangle $XYZ$ is equilateral.

negatives.text:
In triangle $\triangle DEF$,
a) Prove that the internal bisector of $\angle D$ and the internal bisectors of $\angle E$ and $\angle F$ intersect at a point $K_D$.
b) Let $K_D M'' \perp DE$, $M'' \in DE$, $K_D N'' \perp DF$, $N'' \in DF$, and $K_D P'' \perp EF$, $P'' \in EF$. Show that if $K_D M'' + K_D P'' = K_D N''$, then triangle $DEF$ is equilateral.

In triangle $\triangle GHI$,
a) Prove that the internal angle bisector of $\angle G$ and the external bisectors of $\angle H$ and $\angle I$ intersect at a point $L_G$.
b) Let $L_G M''' \perp GH$, $M''' \in GH$, $L_G N''' \perp GI$, $N''' \in GI$, and $L_G P''' \perp HI$, $P''' \in HI$. Show that if $L_G M''' + L_G P''' = 2L_G N'''$, then triangle $GHI$ is equilateral.

In triangle $\triangle JKL$,
a) Prove that the internal angle bisector of $\angle J$ and the external bisectors of $\angle K$ and $\angle L$ intersect at a point $M_J$.
b) Let $M_J M'''' \perp JK$, $M'''' \in JK$, $M_J N'''' \perp JL$, $N'''' \in JL$, and $M_J P'''' \perp KL$, $P'''' \in KL$. Show that if $M_J M'''' + M_J P'''' = M_J N''''$, then triangle $JKL$ is isosceles.

positive_text: \text{a) Find all real numbers } x \text{ such that } \lfloor x \rfloor^2 - x = -\frac{99}{100}.\\\text{b) Prove that for all } a \le -1, \text{ the equation } \lfloor x \rfloor^2 - x = a \text{ has no real solutions}.

negatives.text: \text{a) Solve the equation in the set of real numbers } [x]^2 + x = -0.99.\\\text{b) Show that, for every } a \le -1, \text{ the equation } [x]^2 + x = a \text{ has no real solutions}.
\text{a) Solve the equation in the set of real numbers } [x]^2 - x = 0.99.\\\text{b) Show that, for every } a \le -1, \text{ the equation } [x]^2 - x = a \text{ has no real solutions}.
\text{a) Solve the equation in the set of real numbers } [x] - x^2 = -0.99.\\\text{b) Show that, for every } a \le -1, \text{ the equation } [x] - x^2 = a \text{ has no real solutions}.

positive_text:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $n \ge 4$ and $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ be real numbers such that
$$
x_k^3 = x_{k+1}^2 + x_{k+2}^2 + x_{k+3}^2
$$
for all $k \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, where indices are taken modulo $n$. Prove that $x_1 = x_2 = \dots = x_n$.

negatives.text:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $n \ge 4$ and $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ be real numbers such that
$$
a_k^2 = a_{k+1}^2 + a_{k+2}^2 + a_{k+3}^2
$$
for all $k = 1, 2, \dots, n$, with indices modulo $n$. Prove that $a_1 = a_2 = \dots = a_n$.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $n \ge 4$ and $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ be real numbers such that
$$
a_k^3 = a_{k+1}^3 + a_{k+2}^3 + a_{k+3}^3
$$
for all $k = 1, 2, \dots, n$, with indices modulo $n$. Prove that $a_1 = a_2 = \dots = a_n$.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $n \ge 4$ and $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ be real numbers such that
$$
a_k^3 = a_{k+1}^2 + a_{k+2}^2 + a_{k+3}^2
$$
for all $k = 1, 2, \dots, n$, with indices taken modulo $n$, and all $a_k$ are non-negative. Prove that $a_1 = a_2 = \dots = a_n$.

positive_text: In a unit square, $n > 1$ smaller squares are placed such that the sum of their side lengths is $1$, and any line parallel to the sides of the square intersects at most one of the smaller squares in its interior. Prove that all the smaller squares are axis-aligned with the large square.

negatives.text: In a unit square, $n > 1$ smaller squares are placed such that the sum of their side lengths is $1$, and any line parallel to the sides of the square intersects at most one of the small squares. Prove that all the small squares have equal side lengths.

Inside a unit square, $n > 1$ squares are placed such that the sum of their side lengths is $1$, and any line parallel to the sides of the square intersects the interior of at most two of the small squares. Prove that the small squares are axis-aligned with the large square.

positive_text: Let $\triangle XYZ$ be a triangle and let $R$ and $S$ be points on sides $XY$ and $XZ$, respectively, such that $XR = XS$ and line $RS$ passes through the incenter $J$ of triangle $XYZ$. Let $N$ be the second intersection point of the circumcircles of triangles $YRJ$ and $ZSJ$. The lines $RN$ and $YJ$ intersect at $D$ and the lines $SN$ and $ZJ$ meet at $E$. Prove that the line $NJ$ passes through the midpoint of segment $DE$.

negatives.text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle and let $P$ and $Q$ be points on sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, such that $AP = AQ$ and line $PQ$ passes through the centroid $G$ of triangle $ABC$. Let $M$ be the second intersection point of the circumcircles of triangles $BPG$ and $CQG$. The lines $PM$ and $BG$ intersect at $D$ and the lines $QM$ and $CG$ meet at $E$. Prove that the line $MG$ passes through the midpoint of segment $DE$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle and let $P$ and $Q$ be points on sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, such that $AP = AQ$ and line $PQ$ passes through the incenter $I$ of triangle $ABC$. Let $M$ be the second intersection point of the circumcircles of triangles $BPI$ and $CQI$. The lines $PM$ and $CI$ intersect at $D$ and the lines $QM$ and $BI$ meet at $E$. Prove that the line $MI$ passes through the midpoint of segment $DE$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle and let $P$ and $Q$ be points on sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, such that $AP = AQ$ and line $PQ$ passes through the incenter $I$ of triangle $ABC$. Let $M$ be the second intersection point of the circumcircles of triangles $BPI$ and $CQI$. The lines $PM$ and $BI$ intersect at $D$ and the lines $QM$ and $CI$ meet at $E$. Prove that the line $DE$ is perpendicular to the line $MI$.

positive_text: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $k \ge 2$, and three non-overlapping sets of real numbers $P, Q, R$, each of size $k$. Let $p$ be the number of ordered triples $(p_1, q_1, r_1) \in P \times Q \times R$ such that $p_1 < q_1 < r_1$, and $q$ be the number of ordered triples $(p_2, q_2, r_2) \in P \times Q \times R$ such that $p_2 > q_2 > r_2$. Show that $p - q$ is divisible by $k$.

negatives.text: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $n \ge 2$, and three sets of real numbers $A, B, C$, pairwise disjoint, each of size $n$. Let $a$ be the number of triples $(x, y, z) \in A \times B \times C$ such that $x < y < z$, and $b$ be the number of triples $(x, y, z) \in A \times B \times C$ such that $x < z < y$. Prove that $a - b$ is divisible by $n$.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $n \ge 2$, and three sets of real numbers $A, B, C$, pairwise disjoint, each of size $n$. Let $a$ be the number of triples $(x, y, z) \in A \times B \times C$ such that $x < y < z$, and $b$ be the number of triples $(x, y, z) \in A \times B \times C$ such that $x > y < z$. Prove that $a - b$ is divisible by $n$.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $n \ge 2$, and three sets of real numbers $A, B, C$, pairwise disjoint, each of size $n$. Let $a$ be the number of triples $(x, y, z) \in A \times B \times C$ such that $x < y < z$, and $b$ be the number of triples $(x, y, z) \in A \times B \times C$ such that $x > y > z$. Prove that $a + b$ is divisible by $n$.

positive_text: \text{Find the maximum of} \quad \frac{x+y-z}{x^3+y^3+xyz} + \frac{y+z-x}{y^3+z^3+xyz} + \frac{z+x-y}{z^3+x^3+xyz}, \quad \text{where } x, y, z > 0 \text{ and } x + y + z \ge \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{z}.

negatives.text: \text{Find the maximum of} \quad \frac{a+b+c}{a^3+b^3+abc} + \frac{b+c+a}{b^3+c^3+abc} + \frac{c+a+b}{c^3+a^3+abc}, \quad \text{with } a, b, c > 0 \text{ and } a + b + c \ge \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c}.

positive_text: Find all integer quadruples $(p, q, r, s)$ such that $p + q + r = 2s$ and $\sqrt{pq} + \sqrt{qr} + \sqrt{pr} = s^2$.

negatives.text: Find all integer quadruples $(a, b, c, d)$ such that $a + b + c = 2d$ and $\sqrt{ab} + \sqrt{bc} + \sqrt{ca} = d$.
Find all integer quadruples $(a, b, c, d)$ such that $a + b + c = 2d$ and $\sqrt{a^2b^2} + \sqrt{b^2c^2} + \sqrt{a^2c^2} = d^2$.
Find all integer quadruples $(a, b, c, d)$ such that $a + b + c = 2d$ and $\sqrt{ab} + \sqrt{bc} + \sqrt{ca} = 2d^2$.

positive_text: Let $n \ge 2$ be a positive integer. A grid of side length $2n - 1$ is subdivided into unit squares, forming a total of $(2n - 1)^2$ such squares. Two players, Alice and Bob, take turns (starting with Alice) to mark $2n^2$ vertices with two different colors: Alice uses red and Bob uses blue. After all vertices are colored, they alternately draw $2n^2$ vectors from red to blue points, ensuring all tails and heads are unique. If the vector sum is zero, Alice wins; otherwise, Bob wins. Prove that Bob can always prevent Alice from winning.

negatives.text: Let $n \ge 2$ be a positive integer. A square grid of side $2n$ is subdivided into unit squares. Alice and Bob alternately color $2n^2$ vertices with red and blue. Then, they form $2n^2$ vectors from red to blue points. If the sum of the vectors is zero, Alice wins; otherwise, Bob wins. Prove that Alice can always win.

Let $n \ge 2$ be a positive integer. A square of side $2n - 1$ is divided into unit squares. Alice and Bob alternately color $2n^2$ vertices with red and blue. Then, each of them draws $2n^2$ vectors from red to blue points, one at a time, in any order, with no restriction on the uniqueness of tails or heads. If the sum of the vectors is zero, Alice wins; otherwise, Bob wins. Prove that Bob has a winning strategy.

positive_text:
Let $c, d \in \mathbb{R}$, with $c < d$, be two arbitrary real numbers. A function $g : [c, d] \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to satisfy property ($\mathcal{Q}$) if it is integrable and satisfies the condition
$$
g(x) - g\left(\frac{x+c}{2}\right) = g\left(\frac{x+d}{2}\right) - g(x) \quad \text{for all } x \in [c, d].
$$
Prove that for any real number $s$ there is a unique function $g : [c, d] \to \mathbb{R}$ with property ($\mathcal{Q}$) such that $\int_c^d g(x) dx = s$.

negatives.text:
Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, with $a < b$, be two arbitrary real numbers. A function $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to satisfy property ($\mathcal{R}$) if it is integrable and satisfies the condition
$$
f(x) - f\left(\frac{x+a}{2}\right) = f\left(\frac{x+b}{2}\right) + f(x) \quad \text{for all } x \in [a, b].
$$
Prove that for any real number $t$ there is a unique function $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ with property ($\mathcal{R}$) such that $\int_a^b f(x) dx = t$.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, with $a < b$, be two arbitrary real numbers. A function $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to satisfy property ($\mathcal{S}$) if it is integrable and satisfies the condition
$$
f(x) - f\left(\frac{x+a}{2}\right) = f\left(\frac{x+b}{2}\right) - f(x) \quad \text{for all } x \in [a, b].
$$
Prove that for any real number $t$ there is a unique function $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ with property ($\mathcal{S}$) such that $\int_a^b f(x)^2 dx = t$.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, with $a < b$, be two arbitrary real numbers. A function $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to satisfy property ($\mathcal{T}$) if it is integrable and satisfies the condition
$$
f(x) - f\left(\frac{x+a}{2}\right) = f\left(\frac{x+b}{2}\right) - f(x) \quad \text{for all } x \in [a, b].
$$
Prove that for any real number $t$ there is a unique function $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ with property ($\mathcal{T}$) such that $f\left(\frac{a+b}{2}\right) = t$.

positive_text: Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. On a board are written the numbers $(k^3 - k)$ for all odd integers $k$ in the range $[2, 2n + 1]$. At each step, three numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ are selected at random, erased, and replaced with $\frac{abc}{ab + bc + ca}$. After several such operations, only two numbers remain. Prove that their sum exceeds $16$.

negatives.text: The numbers $2^3 + 2$, $3^3 + 3$, $4^3 + 4$, $\dots$, $(2n+1)^3 + (2n+1)$, where $n \ge 2$ is an integer, are written on a board. An operation consists in erasing three randomly chosen numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ from the board and replacing them with $\frac{abc}{ab + bc + ca}$. Several operations are performed until two numbers remain on the board. Show that the sum of the last two numbers left on the board is greater than $16$.

The numbers $2^3 - 2$, $3^3 - 3$, $4^3 - 4$, $\dots$, $(2n+1)^3 - (2n+1)$, where $n \ge 2$ is an integer, are written on a board. An operation consists in erasing three randomly chosen numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ from the board and replacing them with $\frac{a + b + c}{ab + bc + ca}$. Several operations are performed until two numbers remain on the board. Show that the sum of the last two numbers left on the board is greater than $16$.

The numbers $2^3 - 2$, $3^3 - 3$, $4^3 - 4$, $\dots$, $(2n+1)^3 - (2n+1)$, where $n \ge 2$ is an integer, are written on a board. An operation consists in erasing three randomly chosen numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ from the board and replacing them with $\frac{abc}{ab + bc + ca}$. Several operations are performed until one number remains on the board. Show that the final number is greater than $16$.

positive_text:
a) Let $X, Y \in \mathcal{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ be such that $X^2Y = X$. Prove that
$$
(XY - YX)^2 = O_n.
$$

b) Prove that for each integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$, there exist matrices $X, Y$ satisfying $X^2Y = X$ and with $\mathrm{rank}(XY - YX) = k$.

negatives.text:
a) Let $A, B \in \mathcal{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfy $AB^2 = A$. Prove that
$$
(AB - BA)^2 = O_n.
$$

b) Show that for any $k \le n/2$, there exist $A, B$ with $AB^2 = A$ and $\mathrm{rank}(AB - BA) = k$.

a) Let $A, B \in \mathcal{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfy $A^2B = A$. Prove that
$$
(AB + BA)^2 = O_n.
$$

b) Show that for any $k \le n/2$, there exist $A, B$ with $A^2B = A$ and $\mathrm{rank}(AB + BA) = k$.

a) Let $A, B \in \mathcal{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfy $A^2B = A$. Prove that
$$
(AB - BA)^3 = O_n.
$$

b) Show that for any $k \le n/2$, there exist $A, B$ with $A^2B = A$ and $\mathrm{rank}(AB - BA) = k$.

positive_text: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the set of all functions $g: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying $g(a + g(b)) = g(a) + g(b)$ for all real numbers $a$ and $b$. Find all real numbers $s$ such that for every function $g$ in $\mathcal{G}$, there is a real number $w$ with $g(w) = sw$.

negatives.text: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the set of all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f(x + f(y)) = f(x) + y$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$. Determine all real numbers $r$ such that for every function $f$ in $\mathcal{F}$, there exists some real number $z$ with $f(z) = rz$.

Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the set of all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying $f(x + f(y)) = f(x) + f(x)f(y)$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$. Determine all real numbers $r$ such that for every function $f$ in $\mathcal{F}$, there exists some real number $z$ with $f(z) = rz$.

positive_text:
Let $g_1(x) = d_1x^2 + e_1x + f_1$, $g_2(x) = d_2x^2 + e_2x + f_2$, $g_3(x) = d_3x^2 + e_3x + f_3$ be three quadratic functions with real coefficients and $Q_1 : y = g_1(x)$, $Q_2 : y = g_2(x)$, $Q_3 : y = g_3(x)$ their associated parabolas.

a) Give an example where $Q_1 \cap Q_2 = \{X\}$, $Q_2 \cap Q_3 = \{Y\}$, $Q_3 \cap Q_1 = \{Z\}$, and $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are the vertices of an equilateral triangle.

b) Prove that if $d_1, d_2, d_3$ are non zero and pairwise distinct and $Q_1 \cap Q_2 = \{X\}$, $Q_2 \cap Q_3 = \{Y\}$, $Q_3 \cap Q_1 = \{Z\}$, then $X$, $Y$, $Z$ coincide.

negatives.text:
Let $f_1(x) = a_1x^2 + b_1x + c_1$, $f_2(x) = a_2x^2 + b_2x + c_2$, $f_3(x) = a_3x^2 + b_3x + c_3$ be three quadratic functions with real coefficients and $P_1 : y = f_1(x)$, $P_2 : y = f_2(x)$, $P_3 : y = f_3(x)$ their associated parabolas.

a) Give an example where $P_1 \cap P_2 = \{A\}$, $P_2 \cap P_3 = \{B\}$, $P_3 \cap P_1 = \{C\}$, and $A$, $B$, $C$ are the vertices of a right triangle.

b) Prove that if $a_1, a_2, a_3$ are non nil and pairwise distinct and $P_1 \cap P_2 = \{A\}$, $P_2 \cap P_3 = \{B\}$, $P_3 \cap P_1 = \{C\}$, then $A$, $B$, $C$ coincide.

Let $f_1(x) = a_1x^2 + b_1x + c_1$, $f_2(x) = a_2x^2 + b_2x + c_2$, $f_3(x) = a_3x^2 + b_3x + c_3$ be three quadratic functions with real coefficients and $P_1 : y = f_1(x)$, $P_2 : y = f_2(x)$, $P_3 : y = f_3(x)$ their associated parabolas.

a) Give an example where $P_1 \cap P_2 = \{A\}$, $P_2 \cap P_3 = \{B\}$, $P_3 \cap P_1 = \{C\}$, and $A$, $B$, $C$ are the vertices of an equilateral triangle.

b) Prove that if $a_1, a_2, a_3$ are non nil and pairwise equal and $P_1 \cap P_2 = \{A\}$, $P_2 \cap P_3 = \{B\}$, $P_3 \cap P_1 = \{C\}$, then $A$, $B$, $C$ coincide.

Let $f_1(x) = a_1x^2 + b_1x + c_1$, $f_2(x) = a_2x^2 + b_2x + c_2$, $f_3(x) = a_3x^2 + b_3x + c_3$ be three quadratic functions with real coefficients and $P_1 : y = f_1(x)$, $P_2 : y = f_2(x)$, $P_3 : y = f_3(x)$ their associated parabolas.

a) Give an example where $P_1 \cap P_2 = \{A\}$, $P_2 \cap P_3 = \{B\}$, $P_3 \cap P_1 = \{C\}$, and $A$, $B$, $C$ are the vertices of an equilateral triangle.

b) Prove that if $a_1, a_2, a_3$ are non nil and pairwise distinct and $P_1 \cap P_2 = \{A\}$, $P_2 \cap P_3 = \{B\}$, $P_3 \cap P_1 = \{C\}$, then $A$, $B$, $C$ form a degenerate triangle.

positive_text: \text{Let } x, y, z, w \text{ be real numbers such that } xy(z+w) = zw(x+y). \text{ Prove that} \quad \frac{x+1}{x^2+3} + \frac{y+1}{y^2+3} \ge \frac{z-1}{z^2+3} + \frac{w-1}{w^2+3}.

negatives.text: \text{Let } a, b, c, d \text{ be real numbers such that } ab(c-d) = cd(a+b). \text{ Prove that} \quad \frac{a+1}{a^2+3} + \frac{b+1}{b^2+3} \ge \frac{c-1}{c^2+3} + \frac{d-1}{d^2+3}.
\text{Let } a, b, c, d \text{ be real numbers such that } ab(c+d) = cd(a-b). \text{ Prove that} \quad \frac{a+1}{a^2+3} + \frac{b+1}{b^2+3} \ge \frac{c-1}{c^2+3} + \frac{d-1}{d^2+3}.
\text{Let } a, b, c, d \text{ be real numbers such that } ab(c^2+d^2) = cd(a+b). \text{ Prove that} \quad \frac{a+1}{a^2+3} + \frac{b+1}{b^2+3} \ge \frac{c-1}{c^2+3} + \frac{d-1}{d^2+3}.

positive_text:
Determine all positive real numbers $a$ for which there exist positive real numbers $p$ and $q$ satisfying
$$
p = a - \sqrt{q}, \quad q = a + \sqrt{p}, \quad \frac{p}{q} + \frac{q}{p} = 2023.
$$

negatives.text:
Find all real numbers $a > 0$ such that there exist real numbers $x, y > 0$ with the properties
$$
x = a - \sqrt{y}, \quad y = a + \sqrt{x}, \quad \frac{x}{y} - \frac{y}{x} = 2023.
$$

Find all real numbers $a > 0$ such that there exist real numbers $x, y > 0$ with the properties
$$
x = a - \sqrt{y}, \quad y = a + \sqrt{x}, \quad x^2 + y^2 = 2023.
$$

Find all real numbers $a > 0$ such that there exist real numbers $x, y > 0$ with the properties
$$
x = a - \sqrt{y}, \quad y = a + \sqrt{x}, \quad x + y = 2023.
$$

positive_text: Let $a > 0$. Prove that there is no open interval $(p, q)$ such that $\left|\frac{r + s}{r - s}\right| < a$ for all distinct $r, s \in (p, q)$.

negatives.text: Let $a > 0$. Prove that there is no open interval $(p, q)$ such that $\left|\frac{r + s}{r - s} + 1\right| \le a$ for all distinct $r, s \in (p, q)$.

positive_text: Let $ S = [0, \infty) $, and consider three functions $ p, q, r : S \to S $, defining a binary operation $ \diamond: S \times S \to S $ by $$ x \diamond y = p(x) + q(y) + r(x) \cdot |x - y|, \quad \text{for all } x, y \ge 0. $$ If $ (S, \diamond) $ is a commutative monoid: a) prove that $ r $ is continuous on $ S $; b) find the functions $ p, q, r $.

negatives.text: Let $ A = [0, \infty) $, and consider three functions $ f, g, h : A \to A $, and the binary operation $ *: A \times A \to A $ defined by $$ x * y = f(x) + g(y) + h(x) \cdot |x - y|, \quad \text{for all } x, y \in A. $$ If $ (A, *) $ is a monoid (not necessarily commutative): a) prove that $ h $ is continuous on $ A $; b) determine the functions $ f, g, h $.

Let $ A = [0, \infty) $, and consider three functions $ f, g, h : A \to A $, and the binary operation $ *: A \times A \to A $ defined by $$ x * y = f(x) + g(y) + h(x) \cdot (x - y), \quad \text{for all } x, y \in A. $$ If $ (A, *) $ is a commutative monoid: a) prove that $ h $ is continuous on $ A $; b) determine the functions $ f, g, h $.

Let $ A = [0, \infty) $, and consider three functions $ f, g, h : A \to A $, and the binary operation $ *: A \times A \to A $ defined by $$ x * y = f(x) + g(y) + h(x) \cdot |x - y|^2, \quad \text{for all } x, y \in A. $$ If $ (A, *) $ is a commutative monoid: a) prove that $ h $ is continuous on $ A $; b) determine the functions $ f, g, h $.

positive_text:
a) Show that there exist irrational numbers $p$, $q$, and $r$ such that $p + qr$, $q + pr$, and $r + pq$ are all rational.

b) Suppose that $p + q + r = 1$ and the expressions $p + qr$, $q + pr$, and $r + pq$ are non-zero rational numbers. Prove that $p$, $q$, and $r$ must be rational.

negatives.text:
a) Prove that there exist irrational numbers $a$, $b$, and $c$ such that $a + b + c$ is rational.

b) Suppose that $a + b + c = 1$ and that $a + b + c$ is rational. Prove that $a$, $b$, and $c$ are rational.

a) Prove that there exist irrational numbers $a$, $b$, and $c$ such that $a + bc$, $b + ac$, and $c + ab$ are irrational.

b) Suppose that $a + b + c = 1$ and $a + bc$, $b + ac$, and $c + ab$ are irrational. Prove that $a$, $b$, and $c$ are irrational.

a) Prove that there exist irrational numbers $a$, $b$, and $c$ such that $a + b$, $b + c$, and $c + a$ are rational.

b) Suppose that $a + b + c = 1$ and $a + b$, $b + c$, $c + a$ are rational. Prove that $a$, $b$, and $c$ are rational.

positive_text: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|1 - a| = |1 - b|$ and $|1 - a^2| = |1 - b^2|$. Prove that $a = b$ or $a = \overline{b}$.

negatives.text: Let $u, v \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|u - 1| = |v - 1|$ and $|u^3 - 1| = |v^3 - 1|$. Prove that $u = v$ or $u = \bar{v}$.
Let $u, v \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|u - 1| = |v - 1|$ and $|1 + u^2| = |1 + v^2|$. Prove that $u = v$ or $u = \bar{v}$.
Let $u, v \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|1 - u| = |1 - v|$ and $|1 - u| = |1 - v^2|$. Prove that $u = v$ or $u = \bar{v}$.

positive_text: Find all positive integers $x, y, z$ such that $1 + 2^x + 3^y = 6^z$.

negatives.text: Find all positive integers $a, b, c$ such that $1 + 2^a + 3^b = 6^c + 1$.
Find all positive integers $a, b, c$ such that $1 + 2^a + 3^b = 6^{-c}$.
Find all positive integers $a, b, c$ such that $1 + 2^a + 3^b = 6^c$ modulo 7.

positive_text: \text{Find all integer values of } x \text{ such that} \quad \left( \frac{1 + \sqrt{1 - y^2}}{2} \right)^{\sqrt{1 - y}} = (\sqrt{1 - y})^{\sqrt{1 - y} + \sqrt{1 + y}}.

negatives.text: \text{Find all integer } x \text{ for which} \quad \left( \frac{1 - \sqrt{1 - x^2}}{2} \right)^{\sqrt{1 - x}} = (\sqrt{1 - x})^{\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}}.
\text{Find all integers } x \text{ such that} \quad \left( \frac{1 + \sqrt{1 - x^2}}{2} \right)^{\sqrt{1 + x}} = (\sqrt{1 - x})^{\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}}.
\text{Find all integer } x \text{ for which} \quad \left( \frac{1 + \sqrt{1 - x^2}}{2} \right)^{\sqrt{1 - x}} = (\sqrt{1 - x})^{\sqrt{1 - x} - \sqrt{1 + x}}.

positive_text: \text{Let } n \ge 2 \text{ be an integer and let } x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n \in [1, 2024]. \text{ Show that} \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{x_k} \left( \sum_{j=1}^{k} x_j \right) > \frac{1}{44} n(n + 33).

negatives.text: \text{Fix an integer } n \ge 2 \text{ and let } a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n \in [1, 2024]. \text{ Prove that} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{a_i} (a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_i) > \frac{1}{44} n(n - 33).
\text{Fix an integer } n \ge 2 \text{ and let } a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n \in [1, 2024]. \text{ Prove that} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{a_i^2} (a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_i) > \frac{1}{44} n(n + 33).
\text{Fix an integer } n \ge 2 \text{ and let } a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n \in [1, 2024]. \text{ Prove that} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{a_i} (a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_i) < \frac{1}{44} n(n + 33).

positive_text: Suppose the set $\{1, 2, ..., 2024\}$ is divided into disjoint pairs $\{a, b\}$ such that for each pair, either $|a - b| = 1$ or $|a - b| = 506$. If the pair $\{1518, 1519\}$ is included, find the number that is paired with $505$.

negatives.text: The set $\{1, 2, ..., 2024\}$ is partitioned into pairs $\{a, b\}$ such that for each pair, either $|a - b| = 1$ or $|a - b| = 507$. Given that $\{1518, 1519\}$ is one of the pairs, find the number that is paired with $505$.

The set $\{1, 2, ..., 2024\}$ is partitioned into pairs $\{a, b\}$ such that for each pair, either $|a - b| = 1$ or $|a - b| = 506$. Given that $\{1518, 1519\}$ is one of the pairs, find the number that is paired with $506$.

The set $\{1, 2, ..., 2024\}$ is partitioned into pairs $\{a, b\}$ such that for each pair, either $a + b = 1$ or $a + b = 2025$. Given that $\{1518, 1519\}$ is one of the pairs, find the number that is paired with $505$.

positive_text: A finite set $ S $ of $ n $ points in the plane consists entirely of integer-coordinate points. A segment between two points in $ S $ is called a \textit{longest segment} if its length is strictly greater than all other segments between distinct points in $ S $. Show that the number of such longest segments is at most $ n - 1 $.

negatives.text: Let $ S $ be a set of $ n $ points in the plane with integer coordinates. A segment between two points in $ S $ is called a \textit{longest segment} if its length is strictly greater than all other segments between distinct points in $ S $. Show that the number of such longest segments is at most $ n $.

Let $ S $ be a set of $ n $ points in the plane, all with rational coordinates. A segment between two points in $ S $ is called a \textit{longest segment} if its length is strictly greater than all other segments between distinct points in $ S $. Prove that the number of such longest segments is at most $ n - 1 $.

positive_text: Two circles $\omega$ and $\Omega$ lie outside each other, with centers $M$ and $N$, respectively. One of their external common tangents touches $\omega$ at $S$ and $\Omega$ at $T$. One of their internal common tangents touches $\omega$ at $U$ and $\Omega$ at $V$, and the other internal tangent touches $\omega$ at $W$ and $\Omega$ at $Z$. The lines $UV$ and $WZ$ intersect at point $G$. Let $R$ be the second intersection point of line $TG$ with $\omega$, and let $K$ be the second intersection point of line $SG$ with $\Omega$. The line perpendicular to $GR$ at $R$ meets line $MU$ at $P$, and the line perpendicular to $GK$ at $K$ meets line $NZ$ at $Q$. Prove that $PQ$ is parallel to $ST$.

negatives.text: Let $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ be external circles in the plane, centred at $O_1$ and $O_2$, respectively. One of their external tangents touches $\gamma_1$ at $A_1$ and $\gamma_2$ at $A_2$. One of their internal tangents touches $\gamma_1$ at $B_1$ and $\gamma_2$ at $B_2$, and the other touches $\gamma_1$ at $C_1$ and $\gamma_2$ at $C_2$. Let $B_1B_2$ and $C_1C_2$ cross at $O$. Let $X$ be the point where $A_2O$ crosses $\gamma_1$ and $OX < OB_1$, and let $Y$ be the point where $A_1O$ crosses $\gamma_2$ and $OY < OB_2$. The perpendicular at $X$ to $O_1X$ crosses the line $O_1B_1$ at $P$, and the perpendicular at $Y$ to $O_2Y$ crosses the line $O_2C_2$ at $Q$. Prove that $PQ$ and $A_1A_2$ are parallel.

Let $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ be external circles in the plane, centred at $O_1$ and $O_2$, respectively. One of their external tangents touches $\gamma_1$ at $A_1$ and $\gamma_2$ at $A_2$. One of their internal tangents touches $\gamma_1$ at $B_1$ and $\gamma_2$ at $B_2$, and the other touches $\gamma_1$ at $C_1$ and $\gamma_2$ at $C_2$. Let $B_1B_2$ and $C_1C_2$ cross at $O$. Let $X$ be the point where $A_2O$ crosses $\gamma_1$ and $OX < OB_1$, and let $Y$ be the point where $A_1O$ crosses $\gamma_2$ and $OY < OB_2$. The perpendicular at $X$ to $OX$ crosses the line $O_1C_1$ at $P$, and the perpendicular at $Y$ to $OY$ crosses the line $O_2B_2$ at $Q$. Prove that $PQ$ and $A_1A_2$ are parallel.

Let $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ be external circles in the plane, centred at $O_1$ and $O_2$, respectively. One of their external tangents touches $\gamma_1$ at $A_1$ and $\gamma_2$ at $A_2$. One of their internal tangents touches $\gamma_1$ at $B_1$ and $\gamma_2$ at $B_2$, and the other touches $\gamma_1$ at $C_1$ and $\gamma_2$ at $C_2$. Let $B_1B_2$ and $C_1C_2$ cross at $O$. Let $X$ be the point where $A_2O$ crosses $\gamma_1$ and $OX < OB_1$, and let $Y$ be the point where $A_1O$ crosses $\gamma_2$ and $OY < OB_2$. The perpendicular at $X$ to $OX$ crosses the line $O_1B_1$ at $P$, and the perpendicular at $Y$ to $OY$ crosses the line $O_2C_2$ at $Q$. Prove that $PQ$ and $B_1B_2$ are parallel.

positive_text: \text{Let } x, y \text{ and } z \text{ be real numbers with } xy + yz + zx = 3. \text{ Show that}\\\frac{x^4 + y^4 + (x+y)^4}{x^2 + y^2 + xy} + \frac{y^4 + z^4 + (y+z)^4}{y^2 + z^2 + yz} + \frac{z^4 + x^4 + (z+x)^4}{z^2 + x^2 + zx} \ge 18.

negatives.text: \text{Let } a, b, c \text{ be real numbers with } ab + bc + ca = 3. \text{ Show that}\\\frac{a^3 + b^3 + (a+b)^3}{a^2 + b^2 + ab} + \frac{b^3 + c^3 + (b+c)^3}{b^2 + c^2 + bc} + \frac{c^3 + a^3 + (c+a)^3}{c^2 + a^2 + ca} \ge 18.

\text{Let } a, b, c \text{ be real numbers with } a + b + c = 3. \text{ Show that}\\\frac{a^4 + b^4 + (a+b)^4}{a^2 + b^2 + ab} + \frac{b^4 + c^4 + (b+c)^4}{b^2 + c^2 + bc} + \frac{c^4 + a^4 + (c+a)^4}{c^2 + a^2 + ca} \ge 18.

\text{Let } a, b, c \text{ be real numbers with } ab + bc + ca = 3. \text{ Show that}\\\frac{a^4 + b^4 + (a+b)^4}{a^2 + b^2 - ab} + \frac{b^4 + c^4 + (b+c)^4}{b^2 + c^2 - bc} + \frac{c^4 + a^4 + (c+a)^4}{c^2 + a^2 - ca} \ge 18.

positive_text: Let $p$, $q$, and $r$ be real numbers with $r > 0$, $p \neq q$, and $p + \sqrt{r - p^2} = q + \sqrt{r - q^2}$ (D).\textbf{a)} Show that if $p$ and $q$ are rational, then $r$ is rational.\textbf{b)} Show that if $r$ is a positive integer, then there exist $p$ and $q$, both irrational, such that condition (D) is satisfied.

negatives.text: Let $a$, $x$, $y$ be real numbers with $a > 0$, $x \neq y$, and $x + \sqrt{a + x^2} = y + \sqrt{a + y^2}$ (E).\textbf{a)} Prove that if $x$ and $y$ are rational, then $a$ is rational.\textbf{b)} Prove that if $a$ is a positive integer, then there exists a pair $(x, y)$, with $x$ and $y$ irrational, fulfilling condition (E).

Let $a$, $x$, $y$ be real numbers with $a > 0$, $x \neq y$, and $x + \sqrt{a - x^2} = y + \sqrt{a - y^2}$ (G).\textbf{a)} Prove that if $x$ and $y$ are irrational, then $a$ is irrational.\textbf{b)} Prove that if $a$ is a positive integer, then there exists a pair $(x, y)$, with $x$ and $y$ rational, fulfilling condition (G).

positive_text:
Let $k$ and $m$ be positive integers, and define a sequence $(y_n)_{n \ge 0}$ by $y_n = n^2 + k n + m$.

a) Show that the sequence $(y_n)_{n \ge 0}$ has infinitely many square values if and only if $k^2 = 4m$.

b) Prove that $(y_n)_{n \ge 0}$ cannot contain an infinite arithmetic progression.

negatives.text:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers, and define a sequence $(z_n)_{n \ge 0}$ by $z_n = n^2 + a n + b$.

a) Prove that the sequence $(z_n)_{n \ge 0}$ contains infinitely many perfect squares if and only if $a^2 = 4b - 1$.

b) Prove that $(z_n)_{n \ge 0}$ contains an infinite arithmetic progression.

Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers, and define a sequence $(w_n)_{n \ge 0}$ by $w_n = n^2 - a n + b$.

a) Prove that the sequence $(w_n)_{n \ge 0}$ contains infinitely many perfect squares if and only if $a^2 = 4b$.

b) Prove that $(w_n)_{n \ge 0}$ contains an infinite arithmetic progression.

Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers, and define a sequence $(v_n)_{n \ge 0}$ by $v_n = n^2 + a n + b$.

a) Prove that the sequence $(v_n)_{n \ge 0}$ contains infinitely many perfect cubes if and only if $a^2 = 4b$.

b) Prove that $(v_n)_{n \ge 0}$ does not contain an infinite geometric progression.

positive_text:
a) Provide an example of a finite non-abelian group $G$ with identity $e$, and a proper subgroup $H$, such that every element in $G \setminus H$ is its own inverse.

b) Suppose $G$ is a finite group and $H$ is a proper subgroup of $G$ where all elements in $G \setminus H$ satisfy $x^2 = e$. Prove that if $|G| > 2|H|$, then $G$ must be abelian.

negatives.text:
a) Give an example of a finite nonabelian group $G$ with identity $e$, and a proper subgroup $H$, such that $x^3 = e$ for all $x \in G \setminus H$.

b) Let $G$ be a finite group with a proper subgroup $H$, and suppose $x^3 = e$ for all $x \in G \setminus H$. Prove that if $|G| > 2|H|$, then $G$ is abelian.

a) Find a finite nonabelian group $G$ with identity $e$, and a proper normal subgroup $H$, such that $x^2 = e$ for all $x \in G \setminus H$.

b) Suppose $G$ is a finite group with a proper normal subgroup $H$ where $x^2 = e$ for all $x \in G \setminus H$. Show that if $|G| > 2|H|$, then $G$ is abelian.

positive_text: Let $x$ and $y$ be nonzero real numbers such that $3(x^6 + y^6) = x^2y^2(x^2y^2 + 9)$. Show that at least one of $x$ or $y$ is irrational.

negatives.text: Let $x$ and $y$ be nonzero real numbers such that $3(x^6 + y^6) = x^2y^2(x^2y^2 - 9)$. Show that at least one of $x$ or $y$ is irrational.
Let $x$ and $y$ be nonzero real numbers such that $3(x^4 + y^4) = x^2y^2(x^2y^2 + 9)$. Show that at least one of $x$ or $y$ is irrational.
Let $x$ and $y$ be nonzero real numbers such that $3(x^6 + y^6) = x^2y^2(x^2 + y^2 + 9)$. Show that at least one of $x$ or $y$ is irrational.

positive_text: Suppose $A$ is a $2 \times 2$ complex matrix satisfying $A^{2023} = A^{2022}$. Show that $A^3 = A^2$.

negatives.text: Let $X \in \mathcal{M}_2(\mathbb{C})$ be a matrix such that $X^{2023} = -X^{2022}$. Prove that $X^3 = -X^2$.
Let $X \in \mathcal{M}_3(\mathbb{C})$ be a matrix such that $X^{2023} = X^{2022}$. Prove that $X^3 = X^2$.

positive_text: Determine all positive integers $a, b, c$ such that $2^a - 2^b - 2^c = 2^{10} - 1$.

negatives.text: Find all positive integers $x, y, z$ such that $2^x - 2^y + 2^z = 1023$.
Find all positive integers $x, y, z$ such that $2^x + 2^y - 2^z = 1023$.
Find all positive integers $x, y, z$ such that $2^x - 2^y - 2^z = 1022$.

positive_text:
Suppose $x$ and $y$ are real numbers in $(0, 1)$, with $x$ rational, and for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$,
$$
\{nx\} \ge \{ny\}.
$$
Show that $x = y$.

negatives.text:
Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers in $(0, 1)$, and suppose that for all natural numbers $n$,
$$
\lfloor na \rfloor \ge \lfloor nb \rfloor.
$$
Prove or disprove that $a = b$.

Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers in $(0, 1)$, and assume that for all natural numbers $n$,
$$
\{na\} + \{nb\} \le 1.
$$
Prove that $a = b$.

positive_text: \textbf{a)} Prove that $13m+14$ and $12m+13$ are coprime, for every natural $m$.\\\textbf{b)} Find the number of the pairs $(x, y)$ of natural numbers for which there exists a natural number $m$ so that $\frac{x}{y} = \frac{13m+14}{12m+13}$ and $17x + 19y < 2024$.

negatives.text: \textbf{a)} Prove that $12n+13$ and $13n+14$ are coprime, for every natural $n$.\\\textbf{b)} Find the number of the pairs $(a, b)$ of natural numbers for which there exists a natural number $n$ so that $\frac{a}{b} = \frac{12n+13}{13n+14}$ and $19a + 17b < 2024$.

\textbf{a)} Prove that $12n+13$ and $13n+14$ are coprime, for every natural $n$.\\\textbf{b)} Find the number of the pairs $(a, b)$ of natural numbers for which there exists a natural number $n$ so that $\frac{a}{b} = \frac{12n+13}{13n+14}$ and $17a + 19b < 2025$.

\textbf{a)} Prove that $12n+13$ and $13n+14$ are coprime, for every natural $n$.\\\textbf{b)} Find the number of the pairs $(a, b)$ of natural numbers for which there exists a natural number $n$ so that $\frac{a}{b} = \frac{12n+13}{13n+14}$ and $17a + 19b < 2024$ and $\gcd(a, b) = 1$.

positive_text:
Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. Suppose you are given $n$ real values $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$, not all equal. Define
$$
M = \max_{1 \le i < j \le n} |x_i - x_j|
$$
and
$$
S = \sum_{1 \le i < j \le n} |x_i - x_j|.
$$

Find the minimum and maximum possible values of $S/M$ in terms of $n$.

negatives.text:
Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. Suppose you are given $n$ real numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$, not all equal. Define
$$
d = \min_{1 \le i < j \le n} |a_i - a_j|
$$
and
$$
s = \sum_{1 \le i < j \le n} |a_i - a_j|.
$$

Find the minimum and maximum possible values of $s/d$ in terms of $n$.

Given $n \ge 2$ real numbers $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$, not all equal, define
$$
d = \max_{1 \le i < j \le n} |x_i - x_j|
$$
and
$$
s = \sum_{1 \le i < j \le n} (a_i - a_j)^2.
$$

Find the minimum and maximum values of $s/d$ in terms of $n$.

Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. Consider $n$ real numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$, not all equal. Define
$$
d = \max_{1 \le i < j \le n} |a_i - a_j|
$$
and
$$
s = \sum_{1 \le i < j \le n} |a_i - a_j|.
$$

Determine the minimum and maximum values of $d/s$ in terms of $n$.

positive_text: Let $q$ be an odd prime and $M < 50q$ a positive integer. Suppose $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_M$ are positive integers with each less than $q$, and no number appears more than $\frac{51}{100}M$ times. Assume that $x_1 + x_2 + \dots + x_M$ is not a multiple of $q$. Prove that we can rearrange the $x_i$ into an order $y_1, y_2, \dots, y_M$ such that for every $k = 1, 2, \dots, M$, the partial sum $y_1 + y_2 + \dots + y_k$ is not divisible by $q$.

negatives.text: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $N < 50p$ a positive integer. Suppose $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_N$ are positive integers less than $p$, each value appearing at most $\frac{51}{100}N$ times. Suppose that $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_N$ is divisible by $p$. Prove that there exists a permutation $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_N$ of the $a_i$ such that no partial sum $b_1 + b_2 + \dots + b_k$ is divisible by $p$ for any $k = 1, 2, \dots, N$.

Let $p$ be an odd prime and $N < 50p$ a positive integer. Suppose $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_N$ are positive integers less than $p$, and each value appears at most $\frac{51}{100}N$ times. Suppose that $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_N$ is not divisible by $p$. Prove that there exists a permutation $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_N$ of the $a_i$ such that for all $k = 1, 2, \dots, N$, the product $b_1 \cdot b_2 \cdot \dots \cdot b_k$ is not divisible by $p$.

Let $p$ be an odd prime and $N < 50p$ a positive integer. Suppose $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_N$ are positive integers less than $p$, and each value appears at most $\frac{51}{100}N$ times. Suppose that $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_N$ is not divisible by $p$. Prove that there exists a permutation $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_N$ of the $a_i$ such that for all $k = 1, 2, \dots, N$, the sum $b_1 + b_2 + \dots + b_k$ is not divisible by $p^2$.

positive_text: Let triangle $ PQR $ satisfy $ PQ < PR $, and let $ \Omega $ be its circumcircle. The tangent to $ \Omega $ at $ P $ intersects $ QR $ at $ D $. A line through $ Q $ parallel to $ PD $ meets $ \Omega $ again at $ E $. The line $ DE $ intersects $ PQ $ at $ F $ and $ \Omega $ again at $ G $. On line $ QE $, take point $ N $ such that $ Q, G, F, N $ are concyclic. Let $ S $ and $ T $ be the points where line $ FN $ intersects $ PD $ and $ PE $, respectively. Prove that $ STDG $ is a cyclic quadrilateral.

negatives.text: Let $ ABC $ be a triangle with $ AB < AC $, and $ \omega $ be its circumcircle. The tangent at $ A $ to $ \omega $ intersects line $ BC $ at $ D $. A line through $ B $ intersects $ \omega $ again at $ E $, but is not parallel to $ AD $. Line $ DE $ intersects $ AB $ at $ F $ and $ \omega $ again at $ G $. On line $ BE $, take point $ N $ such that $ B, G, F, N $ are concyclic. Let $ S $ and $ T $ be the points where line $ FN $ intersects $ AD $ and $ AE $, respectively. Prove that $ STDG $ is a cyclic quadrilateral.

positive_text:
Let $a$ be a real number. Prove that there exists a linear function $g$ such that $g(a) = 0$ if and only if $|a| \ge 4$.

We define a linear function $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ to be *useful* if it satisfies:
(i) $|g(x)| \le 2$ for all $x$ with $|x| \le 2$;
(ii) $|g(x)| \ge 1$ for all $x$ with $|x| \le 1$.

negatives.text:
Let $x_0$ be a real number. Prove that there exists a useful function $f$ such that $f(x_0) = 0$ if and only if $|x_0| \ge 3$.

We define a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ to be *useful* if it satisfies:
(i) $|f(x)| \le 2$ for all $x$ with $|x| \le 2$;
(ii) $|f(x)| \ge 1$ for all $x$ with $|x| \le 1$.

Let $x_0$ be a real number. Prove that there exists a useful function $f$ such that $f(x_0) = 0$ if and only if $|x_0| = 4$.

We define a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ to be *useful* if it satisfies:
(i) $|f(x)| \le 2$ for all $x$ with $|x| \le 2$;
(ii) $|f(x)| \ge 1$ for all $x$ with $|x| \le 1$.

positive_text:
Let $ a $ and $ b $ be positive integers with the following condition: for every divisor $ x $ of $ a $ and every divisor $ y $ of $ b $, the sum $ x + y $ is a prime number.

a) Show that if $ a $ and $ b $ are distinct and satisfy the condition, then $ a + b $ is odd.

b) Determine all pairs $ (a, b) $ with $ a \le b $ that satisfy the condition.

negatives.text:
Let $ a $ and $ b $ be positive integers with the following condition: for every divisor $ x $ of $ a $ and every divisor $ y $ of $ b $, the product $ x \cdot y $ is a prime number.

a) Show that if $ a $ and $ b $ are distinct and satisfy the condition, then $ a + b $ is odd.

b) Determine all pairs $ (a, b) $ with $ a \le b $ that satisfy the condition.

Let $ a $ and $ b $ be positive integers with the following condition: for every divisor $ x $ of $ a $ and every divisor $ y $ of $ b $, the number $ x + y $ is a perfect square.

a) Show that if $ a $ and $ b $ are distinct and satisfy the condition, then $ a + b $ is odd.

b) Determine all pairs $ (a, b) $ with $ a \le b $ that satisfy the condition.

Let $ a $ and $ b $ be positive integers with the following condition: for every divisor $ x $ of $ a $ and every divisor $ y $ of $ b $, the number $ x + y $ is a prime number. Suppose further that $ a = b $.

a) Show that $ a + b $ is odd.

b) Determine all pairs $ (a, b) $ with $ a \le b $ that satisfy the condition.

positive_text: Let $\sigma(x)$ denote the sum of the positive divisors of $x$, and $\tau(x)$ denote the number of positive divisors of $x$. Determine all positive integers $n$ such that $\sigma(\tau(n)) = n$.

negatives.text: For each positive integer $x$, let $\sigma(x)$ be the sum of its positive divisors and $\tau(x)$ be the number of the positive divisors of $x$. Find all positive integers $n$ such that $\tau(\sigma(n)) = n$.

For each positive integer $x$, let $\sigma(x)$ be the sum of its positive divisors and $\tau(x)$ be the number of the positive divisors of $x$. Find all positive integers $n$ such that $\sigma(\tau(n)) = 2n$.

For each positive integer $x$, let $\sigma(x)$ be the sum of its positive divisors and $\tau(x)$ be the number of the positive divisors of $x$. Find all positive integers $n$ such that $\sigma(\tau(n)) = n + 1$.

positive_text: Let $X, Y \in M_n(\mathbb{R})$, and define $g: M_n(\mathbb{C}) \to M_n(\mathbb{C})$ by $g(W) = XW + Y\bar{W}$, where $\bar{W}$ is the conjugate of $W$. Show that the following are equivalent: (1) $g$ is injective; (2) $g$ is surjective; (3) $X+Y$ and $X-Y$ are invertible.

negatives.text: Let $A, B \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$, and define $f: M_n(\mathbb{C}) \to M_n(\mathbb{C})$ by $f(Z) = AZ + BZ^T$, where $Z^T$ is the transpose of $Z$. Prove that the following are equivalent: (1) $f$ is injective; (2) $f$ is surjective; (3) $A+B$ and $A-B$ are invertible.

Let $A, B \in M_n(\mathbb{R})$, and define $f: M_n(\mathbb{C}) \to M_n(\mathbb{C})$ by $f(Z) = AZ + B\bar{Z}^T$, where $\bar{Z}^T$ is the conjugate transpose of $Z$. Prove that the following are equivalent: (1) $f$ is injective; (2) $f$ is surjective; (3) $A+B$ and $A-B$ are invertible.

Let $A, B \in M_n(\mathbb{R})$, and define $f: M_n(\mathbb{C}) \to M_n(\mathbb{C})$ by $f(Z) = AZ + B\bar{Z}^2$. Prove that the following are equivalent: (1) $f$ is injective; (2) $f$ is surjective; (3) $A+B$ and $A-B$ are invertible.

positive_text: Find all positive integers $p, q, r, s, t, u$ such that for any two of them, $m$ and $n$, there exist two of the remaining four numbers, $o$ and $v$, with $\frac{m}{n} = \frac{o}{v}$.

negatives.text: Determine all positive integers $a, b, c, d, e, f$ such that for any two of them, $x$ and $y$, two of the remaining four numbers, $z$ and $t$, exist such that $\frac{x}{y} = z + t$.
Determine all positive integers $a, b, c, d, e, f$ such that for any two of them, $x$ and $y$, two of the remaining four numbers, $z$ and $t$, exist such that $\frac{x}{y} = \frac{z}{t} + 1$.

positive_text: Find all real numbers $a$ and $b$ such that: (i) $a \ge 2b^2$; (ii) $b \ge 2a^2$; (iii) $8(a - b)$ is an integer.

negatives.text: Find all real numbers $x$ and $y$ such that: (i) $x \ge 2y^2$; (ii) $y \ge 2x^2$; (iii) $8(x + y)$ is an integer.

positive_text: Suppose $n$ is a positive integer greater than 3. Let $T$ be a collection of $n - 2$ unordered triples of distinct elements from $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, such that for any $1 \le k \le n - 2$ and any $k$ distinct triples $B_1, B_2, \dots, B_k$ in $T$, the union $B_1 \cup B_2 \cup \dots \cup B_k$ has size at least $k + 2$. Does there exist a configuration of $n$ distinct points in the plane such that for every triple in $T$, the triangle formed by the corresponding points has all angles strictly less than $61^\circ$?

negatives.text: Suppose $n$ is a positive integer greater than 3. Let $T$ be a collection of $n - 2$ unordered triples of distinct elements from $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, such that for any $1 \le k \le n - 2$ and any $k$ distinct triples $B_1, B_2, \dots, B_k$ in $T$, the union $B_1 \cup B_2 \cup \dots \cup B_k$ has size at least $k + 1$. Does there exist a configuration of $n$ distinct points in the plane such that for every triple in $T$, the triangle formed by the corresponding points has all angles strictly less than $61^\circ$?

Suppose $n$ is a positive integer greater than 3. Let $T$ be a collection of $n - 2$ unordered triples of distinct elements from $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, such that for any $1 \le k \le n - 2$ and any $k$ distinct triples $B_1, B_2, \dots, B_k$ in $T$, the union $B_1 \cup B_2 \cup \dots \cup B_k$ has size at least $k + 2$. Does there exist a configuration of $n$ distinct points in the plane such that for every triple in $T$, the triangle formed by the corresponding points has all angles strictly less than $60^\circ$?

Suppose $n$ is a positive integer greater than 3. Let $T$ be a collection of $n - 2$ unordered triples of distinct elements from $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, such that for any $1 \le k \le n - 2$ and any $k$ distinct triples $B_1, B_2, \dots, B_k$ in $T$, the union $B_1 \cup B_2 \cup \dots \cup B_k$ has size at least $k + 2$. Does there exist a configuration of $n$ distinct points in the plane such that for every triple in $T$, the triangle formed by the corresponding points has at least one angle strictly less than $61^\circ$?

positive_text: Let $XYZ X' Y' Z'$ be a regular prism with lateral edges $XX'$, $YY'$, $ZZ'$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $YZ$ and construct the parallelogram $XM Y' N$. Let $Q$ be the orthogonal projection of $X'$ onto the line $XN$, and let $l$ be the intersection of the planes $(XN M)$ and $(X' Q Z)$. Let $R$ be the intersection of $l$ with the plane $(XYZ)$. Prove that $R$ is the centroid of triangle $XYZ$ if and only if $XY = XX'\sqrt{2}$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC A' B' C'$ be a triangular regular prism, with lateral edges $AA'$, $BB'$, $CC'$. Let $D$ be the midpoint of $BC$ and construct the parallelogram $ADB'E$. Let $F$ be the orthogonal projection of $A'$ onto the line $AE$, and let $d$ be the intersection of the planes $(ADE)$ and $(A'CF)$. Let $P$ be the intersection of $d$ with the plane $(ABC)$. Prove that $P$ is the centroid of triangle $ABC$ if and only if $AB = AA'$.

Let $ABC A' B' C'$ be a triangular regular prism with lateral edges $AA'$, $BB'$, $CC'$. Let $D$ be the midpoint of $BC$ and construct the parallelogram $ADB'E$. Let $F$ be the orthogonal projection of $B'$ onto the line $AE$, and let $d$ be the intersection of the planes $(ADE)$ and $(A'CF)$. Let $P$ be the intersection of $d$ with the plane $(ABC)$. Prove that $P$ is the centroid of triangle $ABC$ if and only if $AB = AA'\sqrt{2}$.

Let $ABC A' B' C'$ be a triangular regular prism with lateral edges $AA'$, $BB'$, $CC'$. Let $D$ be the midpoint of $BC$ and construct the parallelogram $ADB'E$. Let $F$ be the orthogonal projection of $A'$ onto the line $AE$, and let $d$ be the intersection of the planes $(ADE)$ and $(A'CF)$. Let $P$ be the intersection of $d$ with the plane $(A'B'C')$. Prove that $P$ is the centroid of triangle $ABC$ if and only if $AB = AA'\sqrt{2}$.

positive_text:
A natural number $n \ge 2$ is called $\textit{unique}$ if there exist $n$ positive integers whose sum equals their product.

a) Show that $5$ is a unique number.

b) How many unique numbers are in the set $\{2, 3, \dots, 2024\}$?

negatives.text:
A natural number $n \ge 2$ is called $\textit{special}$ if there exist $n$ natural numbers whose sum is equal to the product of their squares.

a) Prove that $5$ is a special number.

b) Determine how many special numbers are in the set $\{2, 3, \dots, 2024\}$.

A natural number $n \ge 2$ is called $\textit{special}$ if there exist $n$ natural numbers whose product is equal to the sum of their squares.

a) Prove that $5$ is a special number.

b) Determine how many special numbers are in the set $\{2, 3, \dots, 2024\}$.

A natural number $n \ge 2$ is called $\textit{special}$ if there exist $n$ natural numbers whose sum is equal to their product, and all numbers are distinct.

a) Prove that $5$ is a special number.

b) Determine how many special numbers are in the set $\{2, 3, \dots, 2024\}$.

positive_text:
Let $A$ and $B$ be positive integers. Let $T(n)$ be the sum of all positive divisors of $n$, and define $R(n, m)$ as the sum of the results of dividing $n$ by each positive divisor of $m$. Given that $T(A) = R(A, B)$ and $T(B) = R(B, A)$, show that $A = B$.

Is it necessarily true that if $T(A) + T(B) = R(A, B) + R(B, A)$, then $A = B$?

negatives.text:
Define $S(n)$ as the sum of the proper divisors of $n$ (excluding $n$ itself), and $Q(n, p)$ as the sum of the quotients $\left\lfloor \frac{n}{d} \right\rfloor$ for each divisor $d$ of $p$. If $S(a) = Q(a, b)$ and $S(b) = Q(b, a)$, prove that $a = b$.

Is it always true that if $S(a) + S(b) = Q(a, b) + Q(b, a)$, then $a = b$?

Let $S(n)$ be the sum of the divisors of $n$, and define $Q(n, p)$ as the product of the quotients $\frac{n}{d}$ for each divisor $d$ of $p$. If $S(a) = Q(a, b)$ and $S(b) = Q(b, a)$, prove that $a = b$.

Is it always true that if $S(a) + S(b) = Q(a, b) + Q(b, a)$, then $a = b$?

Let $S(n)$ be the sum of the divisors of $n$, and $Q(n, p)$ be the sum of the quotients $\left\lfloor \frac{n}{d} \right\rfloor$ for each divisor $d$ of $p$. If $S(a) = Q(a, b)$ and $S(b) = Q(b, a)$, prove that $a = b$.

Is it always true that if $S(a) - S(b) = Q(a, b) - Q(b, a)$, then $a = b$?

positive_text: Let $b$ be a fixed positive integer. Consider the sequence $(y_n)_{n \ge 1}$ defined by $y_n = \frac{1}{1 + nb}$. Show that for any integer $m \ge 3$, there exist distinct positive integers $p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_m$ such that $y_{p_1}, y_{p_2}, \dots, y_{p_m}$ form an arithmetic progression.

negatives.text: Let $a$ be a positive integer. Consider the sequence $(z_n)_{n \ge 1}$ defined by $z_n = \frac{1}{1 - a n}$. Prove that, for each $k \ge 3$, there are distinct positive integers $n_1 < n_2 < \dots < n_k$ such that the sequence $z_{n_1}, z_{n_2}, \dots, z_{n_k}$ is an arithmetic progression.

Let $a$ be a positive integer. Define the sequence $(v_n)_{n \ge 1}$ by $v_n = \frac{1}{1 + a n^2}$. Propose that, for each $k \ge 3$, there exist positive integers $n_1 < n_2 < \dots < n_k$ such that the values $v_{n_1}, v_{n_2}, \dots, v_{n_k}$ form an arithmetic progression.

Let $a$ be a positive integer. Consider the sequence $(w_n)_{n \ge 1}$ defined by $w_n = \frac{1}{1 + a n}$. Prove that, for each $k \ge 3$, the values $w_1, w_2, \dots, w_k$ themselves form an arithmetic progression.

positive_text: Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. A circular pie is divided into $2n$ equal slices, with exactly $n$ slices labeled $A$ and the other $n$ labeled $B$. Two such pies are considered aligned if they are stacked so that each slice of the top pie aligns with a slice of the bottom pie. Suppose that two pies can be aligned so that more than half of the aligned pairs have different labels. Prove that there exists an alignment in which at least $2\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor + 2$ aligned pairs have the same label.

negatives.text: Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. A circular board is divided into $2n$ equal sectors, half red and the other half white. Two such boards are superimposed. Suppose that for some superimposition, more than half of the superimposed sectors have different colors. Prove that there exists a superimposition in which at least $2\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor + 2$ sectors are red.

positive_text: Let $T_n$ be the triangular region consisting of all cells in the lower triangle of a $(2n + 1) \times (2n + 1)$ grid (including the diagonal). Find the largest number of distinct cells in a path that visits each cell only once, where each step moves to an adjacent cell (sharing a side).

negatives.text: Let $T_n$ be the triangular region consisting of all cells in the upper triangle of a $(2n + 1) \times (2n + 1)$ grid (including the diagonal). Find the largest number of distinct cells in a path that visits each cell only once, where each step moves to an adjacent cell (sharing a side).

Let $T_n$ be the triangular region consisting of all cells in the lower triangle of a $(2n + 1) \times (2n + 1)$ grid (including the diagonal). Find the largest number of distinct cells in a path that visits each cell only once, where each step moves to a diagonally adjacent cell (not a side).

Let $T_n$ be the triangular region consisting of all cells in the lower triangle of a $(2n + 1) \times (2n + 1)$ grid (including the diagonal). Find the largest number of distinct cells in a path that visits each cell only once, where each step moves to an adjacent cell (sharing a side), and the path must return to the starting cell.

positive_text: Let $PQR$ be an isosceles triangle with $PQ = PR$ and $\angle QPR = 20^\circ$. Points $M$ and $N$ lie on segment $PR$ such that $PM = NR = QR$. Determine the measure of $\angle MBN$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$ and $\angle BAC = 20^\circ$. Points $X$ and $Y$ are on side $BC$ such that $AX = YC = BC$. Find $\angle XBY$.
Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$ and $\angle BAC = 40^\circ$. Points $X$ and $Y$ lie on side $AC$ such that $AX = YC = BC$. Find $\angle XBY$.

positive_text: Find all real solutions to the equation $\arccos{x} + \cos[\lfloor x \rfloor] = x$.

negatives.text: Solve in $\mathbb{R}$ the equation $\sin[x] + \arccos{x} = x$.
Solve in $\mathbb{R}$ the equation $\cos[x] + \arcsin{x} = x$.
Solve in $\mathbb{R}$ the equation $\cos[\lfloor x \rfloor] - \arccos{x} = x$.

positive_text:
Determine the positive integers $a$, $b$, $q$ ($a, b \ge 1$, $q \ge 2$, $b$ odd), that satisfy both
$$
q + q^2 + \dots + q^b = a^2 \quad \text{and} \quad \lfloor \sqrt{q} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt{q^2} \rfloor + \dots + \lfloor \sqrt{q^b} \rfloor = a^2 - 5a.
$$

negatives.text:
Find the natural numbers $x$, $y$, $r$ ($x, y \ge 1$, $r \ge 2$, $y$ odd), satisfying
$$
r + r^2 + \dots + r^y = x^2 \quad \text{and} \quad \lfloor \sqrt{r} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt{r^2} \rfloor + \dots + \lfloor \sqrt{r^y} \rfloor = x^2 + 5x.
$$

Find the natural numbers $u$, $v$, $s$ ($u, v \ge 1$, $s \ge 2$, $v$ odd), satisfying
$$
s + s^2 + \dots + s^v = u^2 \quad \text{and} \quad \lfloor \sqrt{s} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt{s^2} \rfloor + \dots + \lfloor \sqrt{s^v} \rfloor = u^2 - 7u.
$$

Find the natural numbers $w$, $z$, $t$ ($w, z \ge 1$, $t \ge 2$, $z$ even), satisfying
$$
